1(5* DecemhrtS.

214

lord 'Lovat's notwithstanding which, there have been found many lu.i>iact"iHu(. wic}jet] an(j ungrateful Persons, who have themselves enjoyed all these Blessings in common with the rest of their Fellow-subjects, and yet have been weak and desperate enough, from time to time, to contrive the Subversion of this happy Establishment, in order to introduce Popish Bigotry and Superstition, instead of the Protestant Religion, and an arbitrary tyrannical Power, instead of a free Government; and as the only Means of establishing and perpetuating those great Evils, to place the Pretender to his Majesty's Crown upon the Throne of this Kingdom: And the more easily to obtain these Ends have,

from time to time, taken Advantage of the Distresses

which, in the Course of human Affairs, have happened to their native Country, to set on foot and prosecute their traiterous Designs:

And whereas divers of the said Traitors to his Majesty have laid hold of the Opportunity arising from the just and unavoidable, but difficult and expensive. Wars, in which this Nation has been for some time engaged, to 1 renew their treasonable Conspiracics, for the bringing

their wicked Purposes to effect, by the Assistance of Troops and Money from his Majesty's Enemies abroad, and by raising a, Rebellion at home:

And whereas by the Instigation of, and in Concert with, the said Traitors, a great Number of French Troops, accompanied by the eldest Son of the said Pretender, were ready, and had in part embarked, and actually set Sail, to invade this Kingdom, in the Year One thousand Seven hundred and Forty-three, but were then prevented from accomplishing their Design by the wife Precautions of his Majesty, and the good Providence of Almighty God:

And whereas the same Traitors, uftless and indefatigable in the Prosecution of their said wic ked and traiterous Purposes, hoping that the , by the great Superiority of their Numb, rs in , might be able to

invade this Kingdom, and at the same time to prevent the Return of his Majesty's Troops from abroad, for the Defence of the Nation, did, in the Year One thousand Seven hundred and Forty-five, encourage the said ekleft Son of the Pretender to his Majesty's Crown to land at that critical Juntture in this Kingdom; who, in pursuance of such Encouragement, did actually land in Scotland, and put hiuifelt at the Head of a large Body of armed Traitors, and cpmmence and carry on, for a considerable time, a cruel, unnatural, and bloody. War against. his Majesty, within this Realm; which has at lust been happily suppressed.

Article I.

Simon Lord Lovat, being a Subject of his said Majesty, One of the said Traitors and Rebels, and conspiring and joining with them in their said traiterous De-ligns, and having withdrawn that due Obedience, Fidelity, and Allegiance, which as a loyal Subject he owed, and of Right ought to bear, to his said present Most Sacred Majesty, the only true, lawful, and undoubted, Sovereign of this Kingdom, his true and natural Lord, did, upon the Thirty-first Day of December in the Year of our Lord One thousand Seven hundred and Forty-three, in the Shire of Inverness, and on the a8th Day ot in the Year One thousand Seven hundred and Forty-five, in the same Shire, and at divers other Days, Times, and Places, wickedly, maliciously, falsly, and traiterously, compals and imagine the Death of his said Majesty.

Article II.

And, for accomplishing his said wicked and traiterous Purpose, he the said Simon Lord upon the said

Thirty-first Day of December in the said Year One thousand Seven bundled and Forty-three, in the Shire of Inverness aforesaid, did traiterously correl'pond with the said Pretender, obtain and accept a Commission from the said Pretender to be a Lieutenant-General of his Foices, and another Commission from the said Pretender to be General of the Highlanders; and did also accept from the

1746*

k

said Pretender a Patent or Grant importing to create him the said Simon Lord Lovat Duke of; and then

and there did traiterously conspire, and enter into an Association, with many other Traitors, in order to raise a War and Rebellion against his Majesty wit jiin this Realm, and to obtain Troops. Money, and Succours, from France, for that Purpose.

Article III.

And the said Simon Lord Lovat did further falsly and traiterously, at the Times and Place before particularly mentioned, and at other Times and Places, assemble himself with divers other false Traitors and Rebels against our said Sovereign Lord the King, being armed and arrayed in a warlike manner, and did raise, and cause to be raised and assembled, great Numbers of armed Men, his Majesty's Subje&s, for the Service of the said Pretender and his said Son, and arrayed, and caused them to be arrayed, in a warlike manner, against: his Majesty; and did traiterously levy, and cause to be levied, a cruel and unnatural War against his Majesty, within this Realm, at the Times and Places aforesaid, in favour of the said Pretender.

Article IV.

And, for the more effectual bringing his said Treasons and traiterous Designs to Effect, he the said Lord Lovat did, in the Month of November in the said Year One thousand Seven hundred and Forty-five, traiterously compose, write, and fend, and cause to be composed, written, and sent, a treasonable Letter to the said eldest Son of the said Pretender, then in Arms within this Kingdom, and joined by, and at the Head of, great Numbers of his Majesty's Subjects, false Traitors and Rebels against his Majesty, then also in Arms and Rebellion against his Majesty, within this Kingdom: In which Letter he the said Simon Lord , among other Things, expressed the great Pleasure it would give him to end his Days in the Service of the said Pretender's said Son; that he was resolved to send to him his, the said Lord Lovat's, eldest Son to venture his Life in his Service, and deliver up his Clan to him; and further expressed and represented his own great Zeal and Attachment to the said Pretender and his laid Sen, and their Cause and Interest, and the Service he had done, was doing, and intended to do, for the said Pretender and his said Son, with Intent and in order to confirm, animate, and encourage, him the said Pretender, his said Son, his Adherents, and all the other said Traitors, in the Prosecution of their laid Treasons and traiterous Designs.

Article V.

And the said Simon Lord Lovat, in further Prosecution of his said Treasons, did, at the Times and Place before-mentioned, and at divers other Times and Places, after the said War and Rebellion began, and while the same was carrying on, traiterously compose, write, and fend, and cause to be composed, written, and sent, divers other treasonable Letters and Papers to divers falle Traitors then openly in Arms in this Kingdom against his said Majesty, and to divers others of his Majesty's Subjects, and other Persons, to allure them of his own Zeal and firm Attachment to the Cause and Interest of the said Pretender and his laid Son, and to confirm, solicit, excite, and persuade, them to engage in, continue, and prosecute, the said War and Rebellion; and to promise and allure them of his Assistance therein.

Article VI

And, the more effectually to attain the End of his said Treasons and treasonable Designs, the said Lord

Lovat did, at the said Times and Place, and at divers other Times and Places, traiterously aid and assist the said Pictender's said Son, and the said other falle Traitors and Rebels, in the earning on the said Treasons, War, and Rebellion, and furnish and provide them with great Quantities of Arms, Ammunition, Implements of War, Clothes, and other Things, useful and necessary for that Purpose; and also sent his eldest Son. and many of his

N ame,

so Ge6. It. l66 — 170 £15

Name, Family, and Dependents, to the Assistance of the said Pretender's eldest Son, and the said other Kebels; and also gave them Advice, Directions, and Ifcftruffions, in the Prosecution of the said Rebellion.

Article VII.

And the said Simon Lord Lovat further, at the Times and Place aforesaid, and at divers other Times and Places, did unlawfully and traiterously hold, entertain, and keep Intelligence and Correspondence, both in Person, and by Letters, and otherwise, with the said eldest' Son of the said Pretender, well knowing him to be so, and also with divers other Persons, who were employed by the said Pretender's said Son; and particularly with John Murray of Broughton Esqirre, Donald Cameron the elder of Lochiel, Donald Carnet on the younger of,

Alexander Mac Lead, Advocate of John Roy

Stuart, Doctor Archibald Cameron, and divers others: all which Persons were employed by the said eldest Son of the said Pretender in this Kingdom, in the said Rebellion; the said Simon Lord well knowing the y

were so severally employed.

All which said Treafims and Crimes above-mentioned were contrived, committed, perpetrated, acted, and done, by the said Simon Lord Lovat, against our said present Sovereign Lord the King, his Peace, Crown, and Dignity, contrary to the Duty of his Allegiance, and against the Laws and Statutes of this Kingdom.

Ot all which laid Treasons and Crimes the Knights, Citizens, and Burgefl'es, in Parliament assembled do, in the Name of themselves, and all the Commons of Great Britain.impeach the said Simon Lord Lovat.

Ordered, That the said Articles be read a Second time. Paragraph by Paragraph.

And the same were read accordingly; and, upon the Question severally put upon each Paragraph, were agreed to by Ihe House to be the Articles of Impeachment of High Treason against Simon Lord Lovat.

Ordered, That the said Articles be ingrossed.

Ordered, That Leave be given to offer a Clause for saving Liberty to the Commons t^exhibit any other Articles of Impeachment against said Simon Lord Lovat.

A Clause was offered accordingly; which was read; and is as followeth; viz.

And the said Commons, by Protestation, saving to themselves the Liberty of exhibiting, at any time hereafter, any other Accusation or Impeachment against the said Simon Lord Lovat, and also of replying to the Anf-wer which he shall make to the Premises, or any of them, or to any Impeachment or Accusation that shall be by them exhibited, according to the Course and Proceedings of Parliament, do pray, That the said I,ord Lovat be put to anl'wer all and every the Premises j and that such Proceedings, Examinations, Trial, and Judgment, thereupon, may be had and used as shall be agreeable to Law and Justice.

J'he said Clause, being read a Second time, was, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

Ordered, That the said Clause be ingrafted with the said Articles of Impeachment.

And then the House adjourned till Tomorrow Morning, Nine of the Clock.

A Petition of divers of the Trustees for put ting in Exc-cution an Act, passed in the First Year of the Reign of Road*, his present Majesty, intituled, An Act for enlarging the Term granted by an Act, made in the 12th Year of the Reign of her late Majesty Queen Anne, for repairing the Highways between the Bear Inn in Reading and Puntfield, in the County of Berks; and for making the said Act more effectual j and for amending Other Road$ in this Act mentioned; was presented to the House, and read; setting forth. That by the said Act several Tolls were granted for repairing the Roads therein mentioned* which have been duly collect!ed, and laid out, for that Purpose, notwithstanding which, the Petitioners have been obliged to borrow one thousand Eight hundred Pounds upon the Credit of the said Act, which still remains unpaid, together with an Arrear of Interest; and which cannot be repaid, and the lloads repaired, without a further Continuance of the said Act, as the same will expire the ift Day of June 1750: And that the several Roads directed to be repaired by the said Act, being upwards of Twenty Miles in Length, the Petitioners, by Experience, find great Inconveniences have happened in executing the Powers given them jointly; which, they apprehend, may be avoided, by appointing separate Trustees for those Parts of the Roads which lead from the Bear Inn in Reading to Seven Mile Stone, and to -field Hatch, and Aldermaston Bridge; and separate Truf-

tees for that Part of the Road which leads from Seven Mile Stone to Speenhamland: And therefore praying.

That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for continuing the Term and Powers granted by the said Act; and for making the same more effectual; or that the Petitioners may have such other Relief as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame* as it shall appear to them, to the House:

Piftemper Sir John Crejfe presented to the House, accordirtg to Order, a Bill to continue and amend an Act, passed in *n e* the last Session of Parliament, intituled, An Act to enable his Majesty to make Rules, Orders, and Regulations, more effectually to prevent the Spreading of the Distemper which now rages amongst the horned Cattle in this Kingdom; and for making the same more effectual: And the same was received; and read the First time.

Resolved, That the Bill be read a Second time.

Way* Mr. Fane, according to Order, reported from the and Mean*. Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider further of Ways and Means for raising the Supply granted to his Majesty, the Resolution which they had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his PI ace; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followed); viz.

Rofolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee,

That, towards raising the Supply grantee': to his Majesty, the Sum of Four Millons be raised by transfem' I.: Annuities, after the Rate of Four Pounds per Cent, per Annum; and that an additional Capital ot Ten Pounds be added to every One hundred Pounds advanced; the Interest of the whole to commence from Michaelmas 1747; that every Subscriber shall, on or bdorc the 24th Day of December instant, make a Deposit of Ten Pounds per Cent, with the Cashiers of the Bank of England; and every Subscriber paying in the Whole, or any Part of his Money, at or before the Time or respective Times that shall be appointed for the Payment thereof, I'uch Sub-ftriber shall be allowed Interest, after the Rate of Five Pounds per Cent, per Annum from the Time of the actual

Payment thereof to Michaelmas next.

The laid Resolution, being read a Second time, was, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

And then the House adjourned till Tomorrow Morning, Nine of the Clock.

Prayers.

A PETITION of the Grand Jury, Clergy, *nd Newcastle Freeholders, of the County of upon Tyne

was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That Road* the High Road from the Town and County of Newcastle upon Tyne to the Town of Belford, and from thence to-Buck ton Burn, in Northumberland, is the High Post Road from London to Edinburgh; and, by reason of the many heavy Carriages passing thereon, is become so deep and ruinous, that Travellers cannot pass along the fame, without great Danger; and that the said Roads cannot, by the ordinary Course provided by the Laws for repairing the Highways of this Kingdom, be effectually amended, and kept in good Repair, unless some Provision be made for raising Money, to be applied for that Purpose: And therefore praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for erecting a Turnpike or Turnpikes between the said Town of Newcastle upon Tjue and, the said Town of Belford, and from thence to Buckton Burn; and for levying such Tolls and Duties, towards; the Repairs of the said Road, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Confederation of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

and also of several Pertoris living in, near* or usually travelling through the Road leading from a Place called Earl's Kiln, in Warrington aforesaid, to the Tojl-bass in Wtllgate, in Wigan aforesaid, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth. That by the said Act several Tolls and Powers were granted for the Term of Twenty-one Years, commencing the First Day of June 1727, for repairing the said Road; and that the better to answer the Intention of the said Act, by carrying on the Repairs of the said Road with Effect, the Trustees, impowered to put the said Act in Execution, borrowed a considerable Sum of Money on the.Credit thereof, and applied the tame, together with the Money arising by the lolls granted, to the several Purposes by the said Act directed; notwithstanding which, l'ome Parts of the said Road intended to be repaired are in a ruinous Condition, in the Winter Season, and such Parts thereof as have already been amended, will, in a ftiort Time, become bad again, if constant Care be not taken to repair the tame; and that the Petitioners, the Trustees, now find the Repairs of the Road aforesaid cannot, during the subsisting Term, be compleated, and the Money at this time due on.ihe. Credit of the said Act repaid, unless the Term and Powers thereby granted be enlarged, and the A ft made more effectual: And further setting forth, That the Roatl leading from EarFs Kill in , to the

Township of Wigan aforesaid, is become so bad and ruinous, that Wheel-Carriages cannot pats in the Winter Seaton, without Danger; and that the said Road cannot be effectually amended, and kept in Repair, unlets some Provision be made for repairing the fame: And therefore praying, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for enlarging the Term and Powers granted and given in

aBd'by the said former Act; and for explaining, and making more effectual the same Act; and taat Provision r may be made- in the said Hill for repairing the Hoad leading from Earl's Kill, in Warrington* to the Toll-bars in the Wallgate, in Wigan aforesaid,

Lord Lovat'i A Message from the Lords, by Mr. Elde and Mr.

Iu.pctl.ment Thurstott.*

Mr. Speaker,

The Lords have commanded us to lay before this House, a true Copy of the Answer of SimoH Lord Lovat to the Articles of Impeachment of High Treason exhibited against him by this House; and to leave the said Copy of his Answer with this House.

And then the Messengers withdrew.

And the said Answer was read; and is as followed); viz.

The Answer of Simon Lord , of Lovat, to the Articles of I mpeachment of High Treason exhibited against him, by the Name of Lord ,by the Knights, Citizens, and Burgesses, in Parliament assembled, in the Name of themselves, and all the Commons of Great Britain.

The said Lord, saving and reserving to himself all Benefit and Advantage of Exception to the Uncertainties and Inefficiencies in the said Articles contained, and also all Advantage and Privileges belonging to him as a Peer of this Realm, in Answer to the afore-mentioned Articles, fays. That being as fully ferifible as any British Subject of the many Blessings these Kingdoms have enjoyed under his present and late Majesty's mild and equal Administration; and having, in the Rebellion of One thousand Seven hundred and Fifteen, given the strongest Proofs of his Zeal for, and attachment to, his late Majesty,' and the Succession of the Crown in his illustrious Family, against such as had undertaken the Destruction of both j he cannot but lament his Misfortune to have his Fidelity questioned at the End of his Days* and him-self, when nearworn out with Age and Infirmities, charged with intending the Subversion of a Government he had, in the Strength and Vigour of his Age, exerted his ut-tnoft Power and Address to support; under this heavy Pressure, attended with many other Calamities and Misfortunes, particularly his own Unability to manr.gr his Defence, his only Resource is in your Lordships Justice, who will, he is well aiTured, regard only plain Fasts, not as aggravated by Skill and Oratory, but as clearly and manifestly proved by the Testimony of credible and unexceptionable Witnesses.

Under this firm Persuasion, therefore, the said Lord, in Answer to the First and Second Articles, denies that he did wickedly, maliciously, falsely, and traiterously, compass or imagine the Death of his said present Majesty, or correspond with the Pretender, obtain or accept any Commission or Comnii (lions, Grant, or Letters Patent, from the said Pretender; or traiterously conspire or enter into any Association whatsoever for raising a War or Rebellion against his said Majesty within this Realm; or for obtaining Troops, Money, or Succours, from , for that Purpose; in Manner and Form as by the said Articles is alleged.

I To the Third Article, the said Lord denies that he did

assemble himself with any Traitors or Rebels; or raile, or cause to be raised or assembled, any armed Men for the Service of the said Pretender, or his eldest Son; or away, or cause to be arrayed, any Person or Persons whatsoever against his said Majesty; or levy, or cause to be levied, any War against his said Majesty in this Realm; in Manner and Form as in this Article is charged.

To the Fourth Article, the said Lord denies that he did compose, write, or fend, or cause to be composed, written, or sent, any Letter, Paper, or Writing, whatso-16

ever to the said Pretender's eldest Soft, to any such Purport or Effect as by the said Article is supposed, or to any other Purport or Effect whatsoever.

To the Fifth Article, he denies that he did compose, write, or fend, or cause to be composed, written, or sent, any Letter or Letters, Paper or Papers, to any Person or Persons, to such Purport or Effetft, as by the said Article is alleged.

To the Sixth Article, he denies that he ever did fumish or provide the said Pretender's eldest Son, or any Traitors or Rebels, with any Arms, Ammunition, Implements of War, or other Things useful or necessary for the Purpose in the said Article mentioned; nor did he fend his eldest Son, or any of his Name, Family, or Dependents, to the Affillance of the said Pretender's eldest Son, or any Rebels whatsoever; nor encourage, advise, direct, or instruct, any of them in the Prosecution of the said Rebellion.

To the Seventh Article, the said Lord denies that he ever did hold, entertain, or keep, any Intelligence or Correspondence with the said Pretender's eldest Son, either in Person or otherwise; nor did he entertain or keep any Correspondence with any other of the Persons mentioned in the said Article, or with any other Person employed by the said eldest Son of the Pretender in the said Rebellion, knowing any of them to be so employed.

And as to all other Matters or Things in the said Articles contained, and which is not herein particularly answered (if any such there be), the said Lord avers, that he is not guilty of them, or any of them, in Manner and Form as laid in the said Articles, or in any other Manner or Form whatsoever j and humbly submits himself to your Lordships Judgment.

Ashley Cozvper, Lovat.

Cler' Parliamentor'

Ordered, That the said Answer be referred to the Committee appointed to draw up Articles of Impeachment, and prepare Evidence, against the said Simon Lord Lovat.

Ordered, That the said Committee do prepare a Replication to the said Answer.

SI R William Middleton reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Grand Jury, Clergy, and Freeholders, of the County of Northumberland, was referred, That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition; and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place, and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, Witnesses were called; viz.

Mr. Edward Bigge, Mr. Geo. Wilson, and Mr. Robert Scott Who, being severally examined, said. That they knew the High Road leading from the Town and County of Newcastle upon Tyne to Be/ford, and from thence to Buckton-burn, in the County of Northumberland, which is about Fifty Miles in Length, and the High Poll Road from London to Edinburgh: That, by reason of the great Numbers of heavy Carriages frequently passing thereon, and the greatest Part of the Soil thereof being a deep Clay, in the Winter Season Travellers on horseback cannot pals along the same without great Danger.

And they also said, That were the several Parishes through which the said Roads lead to perform double the Statute-work thereon, yet the same would prove ineffectual, by reason Materials for amending the same lie at l'o great a Distance from many Parts thereof.

And they severally added, That the said Roads cannot be effectually amended, and kept in Repair, for the Accommodation of Travellers, unless some further Provision be made by Parliament for that Purpose.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for repairing the High Road between Cotv Caw/ey End, adjoining to the Town of Newcastle upon Tyne, and the Town of Belford, and from thence to Buckton-burn, in the County of Northumberland: And that Sir William Middleton, Sir Henry Liddell, Mr. Ord, and Mr. Watson, do prepare, and bring in, the fame.

My Lords,

The Commons have considered the Answer of Simon Lord Lovat to the Articles of Impeachment exhibited against him by the Knights, Citizens, and Burgesses, assembled in Parliament, and do aver their Charge against the said Simon Lord Lovat for High Treason to be true } and that the said Simon Lord Lovat is guilty in such manner as he stands impeached; and that the Commons will be ready to prove their Charge against him, at such convenient Time as shall be appointed for that Purpose.

whom the Petition of the Trustees, whole Names Road*, are thereunto subscribed, for putting in Execution an Act of Parliament, passed in the Thirteenth Year of the Reign of his late Majesty King George the First, for repairing, widening, and amending, the Road leading from Warrington to Wigan, in the County of Lancaster; and also of several Persons living in, near, or usually travelling through, the Road leading from a Place called Ear ft Kill, in Warrington aforesaid, to the Tol -bars in Wallgate, in Wigan aforesaid; was referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition; and had directed him to report the lame, as it appea e I to them, to the House; and he read the Report in tis Place, and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth;

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition,

The Act, of the Thirteenth Year of the Reign of his late Majesty King George the First, was read; whereby it

appeared, that several Toils and Powers were granted for the Term of Twenty-one Years, commencing the lft of June 17 27, for repairing the said Road.

Then Mr. Ralph Taylor laid, That the Trustees itn-powered to put the find Act in Execution have borrowed a large Sunt of Money; and that there now remains a Debt of£.7,4^ 8 upon the Credit of the Tolls, together with Two Years Interest due upon the said Debt: That the Road directed to be repaired is Nine Miles in Length,

Four Miles of which have not yet been repaired; and the other Five, which are at present in a tolerable Condition, cannot be preserved so without a further Continuance of the Act, the Repairs thereof being very expensive, occasioned by Carriage of Materials necessary for repairing tho fame, which Materials lie at the Distance of Four, or even Six, Miles, from some Parts of the Road.

That it will be impossible to repair the said Roads, or to repay the Money borrowed on the Credit of the Tolls, without a further Continuance of the Act.

The same Witness, being examined as to the Condition of the Road leading from Earl's Kill to Warrington, in the Township of Wigan, said, That the same is extremely difficult and dangerous for Wheel Carriages to pass; and, though the Statute-work‘has been conftailtly performed, it is impossible to amend the said Road without the Aid of Parliament.

1. Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That the several Rates and Duties upon Houses, which were granted to his late Majesty King William the Third, by an Act of the 7th and 8th Year of his Reign, as also the several additional Rates and Duties upon Houses, granted to her late Majesty Queen Anne, by an Act of the 8th Year of her Reign, and (ince continued, and made perpetual, shall, from and after the 25th Day of March 1747, cease and determine.

22

in that Part of Great Britain called England, the yearly Sum of Two Shillings, to commence from the 25th Day of March 1747.

3. Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, towards raising the Supply granted to his Majesty, there shall be paid for every Window, or Light, in every Dwelling-house inhabited, within the Kingdom of Britain, which shall contain Ten Windows, or Lights, or upwards, the yearly Sum of One Shilling for each Window, or Light, in such House.

4. Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, That, out of the said Rates and Duties, there be let apart and applied to the General or Aggregate Fund the yearly Sum of Ninety-one thousand Four hundred Eighty-five Pounds and Six Pence Three Farthings, which appears to have been the annual Produce of such Part of the Duties upon Houses applicable to the said Fund, upon a Medium of Five Years last part.

An Amendment was proposed to be made thereunto by inserting, after the Word Lights," these Words, " and lets than Fifteen, the yearly Sum of Six Pence; " and in every Dwelling-house, as aforesaid, which Aiall " contain Fifteen Windows, or Lights, and less than " Twenty, the yearly Sum of Nine Pence for each Win* " dow, or Light, in such House; and in every Dwellinghouse, as aforesaid, which shall contain Twenty Windows, or Lights

And the same was, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

Resolved, That the House do agree with the Committee in the said Resolution, thus amended, That, towards raising the Supply granted to his Majesty, there shall be paid for every Window, or Light, in every Dwelling-house inhabited within the Kingdom of Great Britain, which shall contain Ten Windows, or Lights, and leis than Fifteen, the yearly Sum of Six Pence; and in every Dwelling-house, as aforesaid, which shall contain Fifteen Windows, or Lights, and less than Twenty, the yearly Sum of Nine Pence for each Window, or Light, in such House; and in every Dwelling-house, as aforesaid, which shall contain Twenty Windows, or Lights, or upwards, the yearly Sum of One Shilling for each Window, or Light, in such House.

And the said Lift, and the Title of the said Proposal, were read.

The said Copies of the said Conventions and Treaty are bound up with the other Papers of this Session. And the said Translations, and also the said Proposal, are as followeth; viz.

Provisional Convention of Subsidy between his Majesty the King of Great Britain and their High Mighti-neftes the States General of the United Provinces of the Low Countries, on the one Part; and her Imperial Majesty the Queen of Hungary and Bohemia on the other.

Be it known to all those to whom it belongs. That his Rritamick Majesty, and their High Mightinesse the States General of the United Provinces of the Low Countries, on the one Side; and her Majesty the Emprels Queen of Hungary and Bohemia on the other; being equally convinced of the Necessity which their common Interests have for aconsiderable Reinforcement of Troops in the Low Countries-, and her Majesty the Empress Queen

having made known to his Britannick Majesty, and their High Mightinesse, that Ihe was ready to furnish an equal Reinforcement of her own Troops, provided that (he was assisted by a proportional Subsidy on their Part; the Three High Contractors have thought proper to regulate and settle this Affair between them by the present Convention; and, for this End, they have supplied with their respective full Powers or Authorizations, to wit, his Britannick Majesty, the Sieur Robert Trevor, his Envoy Extraordinary and

VuL. 25.

Plenipotentiary to their High Mightinesse the Lords the States General of the U nited Provinces of the Low Countries;' and their High Mightinesse the Lords the States General, the Sieurs the Count Etienne Randwyck, Lord of Ho-moet and Gaemeren, Knight of the Order of the White Eagle, Grand Seneschal, Judge, and Dyckgrave of Over-betuwe, Droffard of the Town and Barony of of

the Body of the Nobility of Guelderland, of the Quarter " of Nimeguen-, the Count William Ibrd of

of the Body of the Nobles of the Province of Holland and of West Frifeland-, William Buys, First Secretary of the States of Holland and of West; Henry Fan Hoorn,

Lord of Warmenhuijfe, Crabbenkam, and; James

Henry, Count of Rechteren, Lord of Westerveld, Canon of the Collegiate Church of St. Peter, chosen First Member of the States of the Province of Utrecht; Sjeuck Ger-rold Juckema de Burmania, Baron Rengers, Lord of broeck, Grietman of Franckeradetl; Boldewyn Baron Sloet, Lord of Lyndenhorft, of the Body of the Nobility of the Province of Over-TJfell; Tjaard Adrian Gerlaciui; all Deputies to the Assembly of the said Lords States General, on the Part of the States of Guelderland, Holland, and West Friefland, Zeland, Utrecht,

Groningen, and Ommelanden, on one Part; and her Majesty

the Empress Queen of Hungary and Bohemia, the Sieurs Philip des Urftns, Count of RofeBaron of and Graffenftein. Lord of Sonneg, Gricffenburg, Keutfchach Gleis, and other Places, actual Privy-Counsellor of State of their Imperial Majesties, and Hereditary Grand Master of Carinthia, and their Minister Plenipotentiary to their High Mightinesse the Lords States General of the United Provinces of the Low Countries; Thadfe, Boron of Reifchach, Lord of Immendingen and of Chamberlain of their Imperial and Royal Majesties, Counsellor of the Regency of the Anterior Austria, and their Envoy Extraordinary to their High Mightinesse the Lords States General of the United Provinces of the Low Countries, on the other Part; who, after having conferred together, and communicated their respective full Powers or Authorizations, are agreed on the following Articles:

I.

Her Majesty the Empress Queen of Hungary and Bohemia shall maintain, during this Year, in the Low Countries, and shall cause to act, cither offensively or defen-fively, with the allied Army which is there, a Body of Twenty thousand Men of regular Troops, besides that of Fifty thousand, for which her said Majesty is already engaged by virtue of the Convention signed between his Britannick Majesty and her the 10th June 1746; and this additional Body shall be composed of the following Regiments, to wit, of Infantry, of Charles of Lorfaine, Damnitz, Braune, Platz, Bareith, Vruari; of Cavalry, of Batiani, Liehtenftein,' Wurtenburg, Diemar; of Hufiars,

Nadafti, and Ka/nocki. ' -

n.

Her Majesty the Empress Queen of Hungary and Bohemia engages to replace effectually, and without Loss of Time, at her Army on the Rhine, by an equal Number of Troops, all those which (he shall have detached to form the said Reinforcement.

iii.

Article III.

The Body of Bavarian Troops shall, after being reviewed, take the Oath of Fidelity to their High Mighti* nesses the States General of the United Provinces; without Prejudice, however, to the Oath taken to his most Serene Electoral Highness, who reserves expressly to himself the Right of filling up and nominating to thle Commit fions of Officers, and others, which shall become vacant. The Bavarian Troops shall be treated in thofs respects, and paid upon the same Foot with the Republick's own National 'Troops: Their High Mightinesses take upon themselves to provide the Requisitorial Letters for the March and the Return of the said Troops.

Whenever the Generals of the same Rank with those who shall ,lcrvc in the Body of Bavarian Troops shall be called to a Council of War, the Bavarian Generals shall likewise be invited thereto; and, when it shall be agreed to march, the General commanding in Chief the Bavarian Corps shall have notice thereof at the same time with the other Generals.

Article VI.

During the Four Years complete, to reckon from the Day that the said Troops shall be received at by the Commissary of the Republick, they shall be left io the Pay of their High Mightim ffes, to be employed where, and in what manner, the Service of the maritime Powers may require.

Article VIII.

In case the Republick, before the Expiration of the Term agreed on, should have no more Occafim for the Bavarian Troops, and shall think proper to lend them back, their High Mightinesses shall be obl'ged to give notice thereof to his most Serene Electoral Highness Three Months beforehand, and to give them their Pay till they shall be arrived again on the Frontiers of Bavaria, and re-delivered to the Commissary of his must Serene Electoral Highness, who shall be ready to receive them; provided also, that they march, from the Day of their being sent back, by the shortest Route, without halting any longer than the Custom of War allows: And as his most Serene Electoral Highness obliges himself, from the Signing of this present Treaty, to put the Bavarian Troops in a Condition to march in the Space of Four Weeks, and even that the First Divinon, conlifting of Two Battalions, shall set out Twenty Days after the Signing of this present Treaty, it is understood, that, in calc the

Article IX.

In this Cafe, that is to say, from the Time of the Return of the Bavarian Corps into the Pay of his most Serene Electoral Highness, until the Expiration of the Term of Four Years, the Subsidies of 150,000 Banco Crowns shall be augmented by the Sum of 100,000 Banco Crowns; so that the Subsidies are then to amount to 250,000 Banco Crowns, which shall be always punctually paid without the lead Diminution, and in the same Manner, and at the same Times, as has been agreed above in the 7th Article.

Article X.

In Conformity to his most Serene Highness the Elector of Bavaria's, Engagement with her Imperial Majesty the Queen ot Hungary and Bohemia, by the Treaty of the 17th June <.f this present Year, and renewed this Day, to go in Concert, and to communicate, with her said Imperial Majesty in what regards the Affairs of the Empire* and the Preservation of its System; and that particularly with the same View his most Serene Electoral Highness is inclined to second the Intentions of her Imperial Ma-jsfty on the 2d Decree of the Imperial Commission, touching the publick Safety, with his Vote at the^General Diet of the Empire; he hereby reiterates the same Assurances to his Britannick Majesty, and to their High Mightinesses, and promises to execute them faithfully.

Article XI.

The annual Recrufts shall be made on the same Foot as is practised with regard to their High Mightinesse own Troops, so that in like manner the Bavarian Corps is to be paid on the complete Foot of the Regulation practised in the Republick; the Officers shall also be obliged to raise the Recruits at their own Exjicncej for this Purpose his most Serene Electoral Highness expressly requires, that the Commanding Officers of the Corps be allowed to fend, in the Winter, the necessary Orders for raising the Recruits wanting in Bavaria, and also in the Empire.

Article XII.

The Losses sustained in the Field, in Men or Horses, on account of any military Expedition, or of any Foraging, shall be made good upon the same Foot as the Republick makes them good to its own National Troops.

Article XIII.

The Bavarian Generals, and the Officers and Soldiers of the said Corps, who may happen to be made Prtloners of War, shall have the Benefit of the Cartel made with the Enemy, and shall be exchanged against other Prisoners of War, or elle ransomed and redeemed at the Expence of their High Mightinesses: On the other hand, the Prisoners which the Bavarian Troops shall makefepa-rately, or together with other Troops, shall be delivered up gratis to the General commanding the Troops of the Republick.

Article XIV.

The Empire, of which his most Serene Ele&oral High-rvefs has the Honour to be One of the most considerable Members, not being at present at War with any Power, his most Serene Ele&oraiHighness solemnly promises, that

Article XV.

All Deserters, without Distinction, who shall have been heretofore in the Service of the Republ-ck, or of any other Power, and who shall, on the Day of the Review, be found inlisted in the Bavarian Battalions, shall not be reclaimed on account of Desertion: On the other hand, the Chiefs of the Bavarian Regiments, in like manner, shall not have Power to reclaim the Deserters which shall have been in the Service of his Imperial Majesty Charles the 7 th, of glorious Memory, or of his most Serene Electoral Highness now reigning.

Article XVI.

The Rtfwrw//Officers shall not inlist any Deserters from the Troops of the Republick; and the Soldiers,

who shall desert from their Corps after the Review made by the Commissary of the Republick, shall not be engaged, on any Pretence whatever, in the Service of the States General; and when the Magistrates of the Countries, in which the Bavarian Corps shall serve, shall have discovered any Deserters concealed in their Territories or Jurisdictions, they shall be obliged to deliver them up to their Officers: And this Stipulation shall be likewise applicable to the Officers Servants, and to all who shall be in the Service of the said Corps.

Article XVII.

Their High Mightinesse oblige themselves to admit the Bavarian Troops into their Hospitals, and to have them taken care of as their own Troops, provided that they pay the ordinary Contribution, or the Pay, on the same Foot as the National Troops do: The Bavarian Officers shall be permitted to examine, by some among them, in what manner the Sick are treated at d attended, and to make a Report thereof to their Chiefs: It shall also be permitted for the Priests of the Roman Catholick R.Tigion to visit the Sick and Wounded of their Religion, who shall be in the Hospitals, as usual.

Article XVIII.

- At the Departure of the Troops, his most Serene Electoral Highness shall cause to be given to every Soldier Twenty-four Charges, and Fifty to the Artillery for each Piece of Cannon; and, whilst they shall remain in the Pay of their High Mightinesse, there shall be distributed to them, for their Exercises, the same quantity of Powder, Bullets, and Cannon-balls, as is given to the National Troops; and, at their Return, there shall be delivered to the said Troops the same Quantity of Munition as they were provided with at their Departure.

Article XIX.

The Sutlers, and those called Marquetenters, shall be treated, as well in the Field as in Garrison, in the same Manner, and shall enjoy the same Immunities, as the Sutlers and Marquetenters who attend the National Troops of the Repub ick; and their High Mightinesse engage to grant Passports for the Furniture, Arms, and other Requires necessary for the Troops, in order to exempt them from paying the Taxes to the States.

Article XX.

Their High Mightinesse allow the free Exercise of Religion to the Bavarian Troops, as well in the Field as in Garrison, in the same manner as they allow it to their own Subjects; and if the said Troops should happen to be in a Place where there is no Church of their Religion, there shall be assigned them a convenient Place for Divine Service.

Convention for the Campaign of 1747.

Be it known to ail those to whom it appertains, That the dangerousS tuation, and the critical Circumstances, in which the Affairs of the common Cause have been found hitherto, and particularly during the Two last Campaigns, by means of the superior Forces of the House of Bourbon, requiring the moll fciious Attention on the

Part of the allied Powers, and the greatest Precautions, not only to be in a Condition to relict them for the future, but to be able likewise to repair the past Losses, Vox.. 25.

and oblige the Enemy to a just and lasting Peace, in case Treaties with the Conferences appointed at Breda for a general Pacifi- Holland, &c. cation should prove of no Effets, by a continued Series ot Difficulties and Obstacles which France has hitherto thrown in the Way; his Britannick Majesty, always attentive to the Safety of Europe, and the good of the common Caule, having been touched particularly with the Necessity and Importance of chefe very Precautions; has thought he could not better and more lurely attain them than by propohng to his Allies her Majesty the Emprels Queen, his Majesty the King of , and the States General of the United Provinces, to enter into a Concert amongst them to make the inofteffe£tual Preparations, in order to bring great Armies early into the Field, and in a Condition to act vigorously in the Beginning of the Spring.

Upon the Proposition which his Majesty has

cauled to be made to the respective Courts, the Three first Powers have duly authorized their respective Ministers; to wit, his Britannick Majesty, the Sieur Earl

of Sandwich, Villount Hinchinbrooke, Baron Montagu of

St. Neot's, One of the Lords of the Admiralty, his Minister Plenipotentiary to their High Mightinefies the Lords States General of the United Provinces, and at the Conferences at Breda; and her Majesty the Empress Queen of Hungary and Bohemia, the Sieurs Charles Count de Bathyany. Hereditary Lord of Gufng, and of the Lord ships of Sicklos, Bolya, Mofgo, and Yjock, in Hungary, of Neuhoff and Gotenoz in Bohemia, supreme Hereditary Count in the County of Eyfemburg, &c. Chamberlain, Actual Privy-Counsellor ot State of their Imperial Majesties, Viceroy of Dalmatia, , and Slavonia,

Field Marshal, Colonel of a Regiment of Dragoons,

General commanding the Imperial Troops in the Low Countries, Minister Plenipotentiary of her Majesty the Empress Queen of Hungary and for the Government General of the said Low Countries; Ferdinand Count duHarrach, Counsellorot theii Imperial Majesties,

Marshal and Colonel of the Country of Lower Austria, and Minitler Plenipotentiary of her Majesty the Empress Queen of Hungary and Bohemia to their High Mighti-neflls the Lords States General of the United Provinces, and at the Congress of Breda; and Fhadei Baron de Reifchach, Lord of Immendingin and Zimmerholtz, Chamberlain of their Imperial and Royal Majesties, Counselior of the Regency of Anterior Aufria, and their Envoy-Extraordinary to their High Mightinefies the Lords States General of the United Provinces; and his Majesty the King of Sardinia,

to draw up and sign a Convention, stipulating the Forces and Troops which each shall furnish to compose Two Armies, One destined. to act in the Southern Part of France; and another, superior to that of France, to be employed in the Low Countries; and the Subsidies the better to enable them to execute it.

Article I.

For this Purpose, and in order to execute this Plan, the said Ministers, after having conferred together upon the above-mentionedObjects, and communicated to each other their Powers, have, in the Name of their respective Sovereigns, in the First place, agreed. That all Conventions and Treaties formerly concluded between the Three Powers jointly' or separately, and which are actually in Force, and from which the piefent does not derogate, shall have their full and intire Effbt, and shall be reciprocally executed and fulfilled in their whole Extent.

Article II.

As the Ministers of his Majesty the King of Great Britain, and of her Majesty the Empress Queen of Hungary and Bohemia, have entered thereupon previously into Concert with the Slates General of the United Provinces of the Lozv Countries, the RTult of the Conferences held on thisOccasion between the said Ministers and the Deputies of the States General, which is inserted Word for Word in this Act, shall have the same Force as the other Articles of the present Treaty, in whatever concerns their respective Courts.

The said Contingents are to be ready, in order to be assembled to form the allied Army, on the id of March next at farthest; and it is to be underftuod, ".that, her Majesty the Empress Queen shall hold in Readinels for that Purpose the Number of Fifty thousand Men of her Contingent for the said ill of u and the remainingTen thousand Men fHall befurmshed " by her said Majesty in the Course of the Month of " April next, at the farthest.

Article IV.

" Agreeably to the Offers made by the Ministers of " her Majesty the Empress Queen, to verify the effect ive " Number of Troops which are to form the Contingent of her said Majesty, authentick Muster-Rolls shall, from time to time, be furnished to his Britannick Majesty and their high Mightinesses, signed by the Imperial Commanding General, as well of the Recruits, " as they shall arrive, as to shew the real Force of the said C mtingent, in Men and in Horses, which shall be actually preTent, and upon the Places; and, the better " to ascertain the Thing, his Britannick Majesty and their " Hiih Mightinesses (hill have Liberty, either jointly " or separately, to cause tl em to be mustered, as often as " they shall think proper, by Two or more Generals, " whom they thall name for that Purpose; to be understood, however, that her Majesty the Empress shall have the same Liberty with respect to the allied " Troops, if her Impetial Majesty shall require it.

Article V.

" Besides the said Contingents destined for thecom- bined Army of the Allies, the Garrisons must be provided by the respective Powers to whom the Towns or * Places belong; but in such a manner, that Lifts thereof " shall be formed, which shall be, from time to time, transmitted to the General in Chief who shall com* " mand the combined Army; and, if the Necessity

tf should require that the Garrisons rhould be reinforced,

" the same shall be done out of the Troops of the allied Army, belonging to the Power to whom the Towns or Places appertain.

Article VI.

" Whereas the chief Command of the allied Army l* in the Low Countries is conferred by his Britannick Majesty, her Imperial Majesty the Queen of Hungary and Bohemia, and their High Mightinesses, on his

" Royal Highness the Duke of , the follow-

ing Articles are agreed on to serve for a Rule on that Occasion

Article I.

" The chief Command of the Army of the Allies in the Low Countries being conferred by his Britannick Majesty, her Imperial Majesty the Queen of Hungary " and Bohemia, and their High Mightinesses, on his " Royal Highness the Duke of the Generals

" and the Troops who shall composethat Army shall be " under the Orders of his Royal Highness during the " next Campaign.

Article II.

" The General commanding in chief shall, in every thing which regards the Operations of the War, ‘and " the Good of the common Cause, consult with the chief " General of each Body of the allied Troops that are " under his Command; which Generals may consult with the Generals of those Troops under their Command, upon the Matters proposed, whenever they shall find it necessary.

Art'de III.

" When the General commanding in chief shall thtnjc " proper to call a Council of War, that Council shall " c- nlift of Generals or Officers cfeach Natron, of equal " Rank.

Article IV.

" The Orders which the G.neral commanding in chief " shall give the Troops that shall compose the allied " Arm'1, shall bedi.eAcd to the General who (hallcommand each Cotps, as far as the Service can permit the " fame. *

Article V.

" The Detail of their Troops shall be left to the Generals of each Corps.

Article VI.

" The Troops of the combined Army of the different " Nations shall be tieated, with regard to the Service, " upon one and the same Foot, and shall enjoy equally " Quarters, and other Advantages.

' Article VII.

" As to the Rank and Service of the Generals, and " other tuch like Articles, the same Method shall be " followed as was praiftiled in the War finished by the " Peace of Utrecht.

Article VIII.

t: The said General commanding in chief shall act in " Concei t with the General commanding the Troops of " the States General of the United Provinces in the allied " Army, in all that shall relate to the Security of the " Frontiers of the Republick; and, if he finds necessary " to draw Troops of his Britannick Majesty, or of her " Imperial Majesty, out of the Places of the State where " they are at present, or where they may be received " hereafter, he shall not fend the Orders and Warrants " directly to the Officers commanding the Regiments, * nor even to the Governors of the Places, but shall direct them to the States General, that they may join " their Warrants thereto in the usual Form, when it " shall be found necessary to draw Troops out of Places " in Brabant and Flanders, which are of the Sovereignty " of the United Provinces; but if it shall be found " necessary to draw them out of Places situated in the " fiid Provinces, there must be a Warrant from the States " of the Province, besides that of the States General; and " the said Troops shall be obliged, in their Marches, to " follow the Orders contained in the Warrants, and the " Routes which shall be given them.

Article HI.

Her Majesty the Empress shall, besides what is mentioned in the preceding Helult, furnish a Body of Sixty thousand effective Men, which shall act in the Southern Part ot France.

Arc! his Majesty the King of Sardinia shall have a Body of Thirty thousand effective Men to act jointly with the Imperial Army in France.

Article IV.

Her Majesty the Empress, and his Majesty the King of Sardinia, shall moreover entertain a sufficient Number of Troops in Italy ready and in a Condition to act, to the end that the Possessions of their Majesties may be secured, and that the King of Spain may have room to apprehend a future Entcrpriz- against the Kingdom of Naples and Sicily, in case his Catholick Majesty should not make Peace with his Britannick Majesty and h>s Allies: It is however understood, that there shall not, upon any Cun-(ideration, be diminished from the Numbtrot Sixty thousand Imperialists and Thirty thousand , which

are, as it is laid ab ve, to act in France.

His Britannick Majesty shall furnish Ships

of War, which shall second and support the Ofierations of the combined Army in every thing which may favour the Interest of the Allies in the Southern Part of , and on the Coasts of Italy; and his Sardinian Majesty engages himself to employ his Gailies to favour those same Objects.

Her Majesty the Empress shall certify to her Allies the Number of her Troops in the Southern Part of,

as also of those that shall remain in Italy, by the Commu-Vbl. 25.

Article V.

To enable ber Majesty the Empress Queen to bear (a great an Expence, and the better to put her in a Condition to make the above Efforts, and to fulfil her Engagements, his Britannick Majesty engages himself to cause to be paid to her said Majesty a Subsidy of Four hundred thousand Pounds Sterling for this Year.

Article VI.

That Sum shall be paid in the City of London, into the Hands of the Sieur de H'afner, her Imperial Majesty's M inifter, or to the Person or Persons authorized by the Emprcls to receive the same.

One hundred and Fifty thousand Pounds Sterling shall be paid on the Twenty-fourth of this Month, to put the Troops of her Majesty the Empress in a Condition to act at the Time fixed, of the Firstof March, and the Course of the Month of April; and the other Payments shall be made as follows, viz. On the last Day of February, Fifty thousand Pounds Sterling; on the last Day of March,

Fifty thousand Pounds Sterling; and, finally, Fifty thousand Pounds Sterling the last Day of April-, the Payment of the last One hundred thousand Pounds Sterling shall be made when the Sixty thousand Men destined for the Campaign of the Netherlands shall be declared complete by the Certificate of the Generals named for the Mustering of them; and, in case they are nt so at the End of the Month of April, his Britannick Majesty shall not be engaged towards her Imperial Majesty fora higher Subsidy than that of Three hundred thousand Pounds Sterling.

Article VII.

And whereas likewise the King of Sardinia must make extraordinary Efforts on his Side to furnish hisContingent ot Troops in the Army that is to act in France in One or more Bodies, as shall be judged the most advantageous for the Good of Affairs; and to have at the same time the necessary Troops for Italy, as well as those that are to guard his Frontiers on the Side of Savoy and {

his Britannick Majesty obliges himself to pay him the Subsidy ot Three hundred thousand Pounds Sterling, which shall be paid to him proportionally in Advance, and at the same Terms, and with the same Facilities, promised to her Majesty the Empress, and ilipulated in the present Convention, Article 6th.

Article VIII.

Several Provinces of the Republick having hot yet paid their respect ive Quota Parts or the Subsidy of an Hundred and Fifty thousand Pounds Sterling, granted by the Convention of the Thirty-first of August 1746, his Majesty the King of Great Britain shall act jointly with her Majesty :he Empress Queen, to induce these Provinces to made good immediately their Engagements.

His Majesty, having given his Consent to a further Con-ventiunforan additional Subsidy of Fifty thousand Pounds Sterling, shall caulc lo be paid from henceforth his Two-thirds, making Thirty-three thousand Three hundred and Thirty-three Pounds and One-third Sterling; and shall endeavour effectually to engage the Republick to fulfil this Convention as (oon as possible* and to pay with the same Readiness its Quota Part.

Article IX.

This Treaty shall be ratified by their said Majesties, and the Ratifications shall be exchanged within the Space of Six Weeks, or sooner, if possible.

In Testimony whereof, we the said Ministers hav®

signed the present Treaty with our own Hands, and have set thereto the Seal of our Arms.

Whereas a Body of his Majesty's Electoral Troops, fconfifting of 5,000 Horle and 13,000 Foot, were taken into the Pay of Great Britain, to act in the Low Countries with the Aujirian Troops, and those of the States General of the United Provinces, until the 2 5th Day of 'November 1746; since which time his Majesty thought itadviseable, for the Service of the common Cause, to continue the said Troops in the Low Countries at his own Expence, to the end that they might be the more ready, upon any extraordinary Occasion, to take the Field early in the Spring: And whereas it is fotind necessary, that a like Body of Troops should be continued for the Year *747, towards completing Forty thousand Men which Great Britain is to maintain in the Low Countries, to act as aforesaid, his Majesty, in Consideration of the great Difficulties there are to obtain such a Number of Men for this Purpose, does propose to continue the said Five thousand Horse and Thirteen thousand Foot to act in the Low Countries for the Year 1747, on the following Conditions; that is to say.

That there be granted to his Majesty, for defraying the Expence of the Pay and Subsistence of the said Body of Troops, to conlift of Five thousand Horse and Thirteen thousand Foot, the Sum of Four hundred thousand Pounds Sterling.

That the said Troops be allowed to march back into his Majesty's Ele&ora] Dominions on the 25th Day of November in this present Year, in case no previous Agreement shall be made for their remaining in the Low Countries.

That in case his Majesty's Electoral Dominions should be attacked or invaded, his Majesty be at Liberty to order the said Troops to march back immediately for the Defence of the fame.

And as it is thought necessary that a Train of Artillery should attend the above-mentioned Troops, his Majesty will furnish the fame, on the Payment of an additional Sum of Ten thousand Pounds Sterling.

A Petition of the several Freeholders and Inhabitants within the County of Durham, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, was presented to the House, and read) letting forth. That the High Road leading from Sunderland, near the Sea, to the City of Durham, in the County of Durham, by reason of the Deepneis of the Soil, and many heavy Carriages passing along the fame, is become, very ruinous, and much out of Repair, and, in the Winter Season, many Parts thereof are so bad, that Coaches* Waggons, and other Carriages, cannot pass along the same without D nger: And therefore, in regard the said Road cannot, by the ordinary Course appointed by the Laws and Statutes of this Realm, be effectually amended without the Aid of an Act of Parliament (the Inhabitants of the several Parishes, through which the said Road leads, being not of Ability to amend the lame), praying. That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for repairing and amending the Road aforesaid, by such Means, and in such Manner, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee, to whom the other Petition of the several Freeholders and Inhabitants within the County of Durham, whose Names are thereunto lub-feribed, is referred: And that they do examine the Matter thereof) and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House.

A Petition of Peter Shaw, Doctor in Physick, and others, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, Creditors of the Company of Mercers of London, on behalf of themselves, and the rest of the Creditors, Subscribers for Annuities, and Annuitants of the said Company, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth. That the Mercers of London were incorporated by Letters Patent of King Richard the Second, for the better providing a Support for the Poor of the said Mystery; and afterwards, by Letters Patent of King Henry the Eighth, were impowered to have and use a Common Seal for the Business of the said Corporation: That his late Majesty King Charles the Second, by his Letters Patent, was pleased to vest the Care and Power of managing the Affairs of the said Company in a Court of Assistants: That, in or about the Year 1699, the said Company fraudulently established, and till the latter End of the Year 1745 kept on Foot, a Scheme for secur'ing Annuities to the Widows of such Persons as should subscribe and pay for the fame; but, being at that time very considerably indebted, instead of making a Capital of the said Subscrip-tioa Money, and improving the same (which would have been more than a sufficient Fund for the said Annuities), applied great Part thereof to the Discharge of their said Debt, without the Consent or Privity of the Subscribers or Annuitants; and by such Mrfapplication, or byfome other Mismanagement, so totally exhausted the said Sub-fcr'iption Money, that, in or about the Year 1725, they were obliged to raise Two thousand Pounds to pay the Annuities due at Lady-day: That the Court of Assistants of the said Company haring thereupon appointed a Standing Committee, a few of their own Members, to inspect and examine the said Company's Books and Accounts, and to direct the Payment of their Money, the said Committee fraudulently kept up the said Company's Credit, and unwarrantably took up considerable Sums, not only by Sub-feriptions for Annuities, but by way of Loan, on the Company's Common Seal, without ever once reporting either to the General Court, or Court of Assistants, a true State of the Company's Affairs or Circumstances, or of their ©wa. That there hath be?n Time out of Mind a Sea Port, or Harbour for Shipping, at Southwould aforesaid, which is now become almost use-lcfs, by reason that the Haven, which leads into the said Port or Harbour, is so choukcd up with Sand, that even very small Ships cannot get in or out of toe said Port or Harbour; which isnot onlyprejudici.il to the said Borough of Southwould, and the Neighbouring Country, but also to the Navigation of his Majesty's Slops, and those of his Subjects; the said Harbour having been formerly found very commodious for the Prel'ervation of the Ships of this Nation, either Northwards, or Southward bound, and likewise very convenient for Exporting and Importing of Com, Grain, Coals, and Merchandizes of divers Kinds: That the Petitioners conceive it is for publick Benefit to have as many good and safe Ports and Harbours within this Nation as conveniently can be; and that the Charge of opening, and clearing away the Sand which obstructs the Navigation into, and out of, the said Port of Harbour, and of keeping the same open, w ill require larger Sums of Money than the said Bailiffs and Commonalty can raise for that Purpose: And therefore praying. That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to enable Trustees, in such Bill to be named, to clear away and remove such Banks of Sand as at present obstruct the Navigation into, and out of, the said Port or Harbour, and to use other proper Means for keeping the said Haven open, and for rendering the said Harbour ulerul; and for laying a small Duty upon such Ships as shall put into the said Port, and upon such Goods as shall be shipped off or landed there, to enable such Trustees to carry on the said Undertaking.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Mattel thereof; a.id report the lame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

An Amendment was proposed to be made to the said Amendment, by inserting, after " Great ," these

Words, " or in any of the Inns of Court or Chancery

And the Question being put. That those Words be inserted in the said Amendment;

It passed in the Negative.

Then the said Amendment was, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

Then the Question being put, That the Clause in the Bill, Folio. 20. relating to the Universities,. Hand Part of the Bill.

It passed in the Negative.

and Advantage to the Petitioners, and their Neighbours:

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act for repealing the several Rates and Duties upon Houses, Windows, and Lights, and for granting to his Majesty other Rates and Duties upon Houses, Windows, or Lights; and for raising the Sum of Four Millions Four hundred thousand Pounds by Annuities to be charged on the said Rates and Duties; without any Amendment: And also.

The Lords have agreed to the Bill, intituled, An Act to continue, explain, and amend, an Act, made in the last Session of Parliament, intituled, An Act to enable his Majesty to make Rules, Orders, and Regulations, more effectually to prevent the Spreading of the Distemper which now rages amongst the horned Cattle in this Kingdom; without any Amendment: And also,

The Lords have passed a Bill, intituled, An Act to enable Edmund Garforth, formerly called Edmund,

and his Heirs, to take, use, and bear, the Surname and Arms of Garforth: To which the Lords desire the Concurrence of this House: And also,

The Lords have passed a Bill, intituled, An Act for raising Money by Leafing or Sale of the Estates late of Thomas Taylor Esquire, the Father, and Thomas Taylor Esquire, the Son, deceased, to discharge the Debts and Incumbrances affecting the lame; and for making a Partition of such Estates, or so much thereof as shall not be fold, for the Purposes aforesaid: To which the Lords desire the Concurrence of this House.

Mr. Bowes reported from the Committee* to whom the Petition of the Freeholders and Inhabitants of the Counties of York and Durham, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, was referred, That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition; and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk'sTable: Where the lamb was read; and is as follower h; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition,

The Agent for the Petitioners called son and Mr. John Reynoldson: Who, being severally examined, laid, That they are well acquainted with the Road leading from Catterick Bridge, in the county of ,

through Farm, in the said County, to and through Stock-ton, in the County of Durham', and from thence to Sedge-field, in the said County of Durham, to the City of Durham; which is a common High Road, and is so far out of Repair, as to be extremely dangerous for Wheel-Carriages: That the several Parillies, through which the said Road leads, have constantly performed the Statute-work, which has been found inefficient to keep the said Roads in Repair, and that it is inapoflible to amend the Road without the Aid of an Act of Parliament.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for repairing the Roads leading from Bridge, in the County of York, through Far, in the said County, to and through Stockton, in the County of Durham, and from thence, through Sedgefield, to the City of Durham: And that Mr. Bowes, Mr. Fane, Mr. Lambton, Sir George Oxenden, Sir Miles Stapyiton, Mr. Turner, Mr. Comptroller, Mr. Tempest, and Mr. John Forke, do prepare, and bring in, the lame.

Mr. Fane reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Justices of the Peace, Gentlemen, Freeholders, and Inhabitants, within the County Palatine of Durham, whole Names are thereunto subscribed, was referred, that the Committee had examined the Matter of the said Petition; and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the feme was read; and is as followeth viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition, the following Witnesses were called;

Mr. George Arrowjmith and Mr. John Gibson: Who, being severally examined, said, That the High Road leading from the Town of Stockton to Barnard Castle, through Darlington, in the said County, by reason of the Deepnefe of the Soil, and many heavy Carriages frequently passing along the feme, many Parts thereof are become so ruinous, and out of Repair, that, in the Winter Sealoo* Coaches, Waggons, and other Carriages, cannot pass without great Danger.

And they further feid. That the said Road cannot, by the ordinary Course appointed by the Laws and Statutes of this Realm, for repairing the Highways of this Kingdom, be effectually amended, and kept in good Repair, fit for the Accommodation of Travellers, unless some further Provision be made by Parliament for that Purpose.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for repairing the High Road from the Town of Stockton upon Tees, in the County of Durham, through Darlington, to Barnard-Castle, in the same County: And that Mr. Vane, Mr. Bowes, Mr. Lambton, Mr. Tempest, Sir Henry Liddell, and Mr. Shultleworth, do prepare, and bring in, the feme.

A Petition of the Commissioners for building a Bridge at Westminster being offered to be presented to the House;

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer, by his Majesty's Command, acquainted the House, That his Majesty, having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House:

Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; letting forth. That the Petitioners are, by several Acts of Parliament passed in his present Majesty's Reign, appointed Commissioners for building a Bridge cross the River Thames, from the City of Westminster, to the oppose Shore in the County of Surrey; and are, by Two Acts passed in the 12th and 13th Years of his present Majesty's Reign, impowered to make, design, and lay out, such Ways, Streets, and Passages, as they shall find proper to make, open, and lay out, on each Side the River Thames, to and from the said intended Bridge, the Courts of Justice, both Houses of Parliament, and the Parts adjacent; and to agree for and purchase such Houses and Ground, within certain Limits by the said Acts prescribed, as they shall find necessary for them to be possessed of: That the Petitioners have made a considerable Progress in building the said Bridge; and have purchased several Houses and Parcels of Ground for opening, widening, and rendering convenient, the said Ways, Streets, and

*7

Passages; in doing which they have expended almost all the Monies hitherto granted them for the said Purposes, notwithstanding the y have proceeded with the utmost Care and Frugality; and are still under Contrafts for feve- . ral Parts of the Works which are now carrying on, and which will amount to a greater Sum than is now in the Hands of the Petitioners; and that the Petitioners find themselves under a Necessity of applying to this House for such further Sums of Money as this House shall judge proper, that a Work so useful and advantageous to the Publick may not be Hopped for want thereof: And therefore praying the House will take the Premises into Consideration, and grant the Petitioners such further Sums of Money as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee of the whole House, to whom it is referred to consider further of the Supply granted to his Majesty.

A Petition of John Wadsworth was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That, in the Beginning of King William's War with France, we made use of

common Paper for Cartridges, both for the Royal Navy and Train of Artillery; but that, when we came to engage, there often happened to be Part ofa Cartridge left in the Guns, which kept a Coal of Fire, so that the next Cartridge took Fire, and the Gun went off, before the Men could charge, or get clear of the Gun, by which manyMenloft their Limbs or Lives; that when they came to engage, after the first Firing, none would venture to charge the Guns till they had fponged them, which took up a great deal of Time; but that th having found

out the Use of Parchment for Cartridges, which kept no Coal of Fire, had no Occasion to sponge their Guns; which enabled them to fire Twice to our Once, and gave them great Advantages in all Engagements; but that, in Queen Anne's War, we made use of Parchment, which retained no Coal of Fire; but that, as Parchment has a greasy Quality from the Skin, which uncorns the Powder, and the Nitre in the Powder, rots the Skin, which de-ftroys both in a short Time; for this Reason the Gunners of the Royal Navy durst not fill Parchment Cart-tridges with Powder before they had Occasion to use them, for Fear of having both Cartridge and Powder spoiled: That to remedy these Inconveniences, the Petitioner, being concerned in making Paper, did let himself at work to find out a Way of curing Paper for Cartridges, in retaining no Coal of Fire, and also topreserve the Powder much longer than the Powder Barrels will keep it good: That after a Multitude of Experiments, long Application, and great Expence, he did, in the Year 1711, discover what he fought for, and presented his cured Paper to the Board of Ordnance; but that it was not made use of until the Year 1724, when, after Two Years Trial, and being found to answer the Ends aforesaid, the cured' Cartridges of his Invention came into general Use, and have been ever since used both for the Royal Na\y and Train of Artillery; so that for Twenty-two Years pall he hath saved the Government Five Parts in Six of the
