Honourable William Hall Gage Esquire, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That, at the last Election of Barons to serve in this present Parliament for the Town and Port of Seaford, in the County of Sussex, the Petitioners, together with the Right honourable liam Pitt Esquire and William Hay Esquire, were Candidates: That, on the Day before the said Election, a noble Peer of this Realm did invite to, and entertain at, his House, most of the Voters fur the said Town and Port; and, in the Room where they were assembled, spake to them one by one, and did sollicit and influence them with respect to giving their Votes at the said Election; by ' means whereof several Persons, who had promised to vote, and would have voted, for the Petitioners, were prevailed upon by the said noble Peer to vote for the said Mr. Pitt and Mr Hay; which Proceeding, the Petitioners

conceive, is an high Infringement of the Liberties and Privileges of the Commons of Great Britain: That, on the Day of th'e Election, in order to awe and influence the Voters in favour of the Sitting Members, and deter them from voting for the Petitioners, the said noble Peer came into the Court, accompanied by other Peers of the Realm; and, being seated near to the Returning Officer, did continue there until the Poll was closed; notwithstanding the Presence of him, and the said other Peers, was objected to by One of the Petitioners, and the Returning Officer applied to by him not to take the Poll while the said Peers remained present in the Court; in all which the said Petitioner thought himself fully justified, as he apprehended their Presence obstructed the Freedom of the Election, and, from the several declared Resolutions of the House of Commons, was a Violation of the Rights and Privileges of the Commons of Great Britain; and that by thele, and other illegal Practices, the Petitioners loft a great Number of Votes, which would otherwise have been given for the Petitioners: And therefore praying the House to take the Premises into Consideration; and to grant the Petitioners such Relief as to the House shall seem meet.

The House was moved, That the Resolutlon of the House, of the Sixteenth Day of this instant November

" That it is an high Infringement of the Liberties and " Privileges of the Commons of Great Britain, for any " Lord of Parliament, or any Lord Lieutenant of any " County, to concern themselves in Elections of Members to lerve for the Commons in Parliament," might be read:

And the feme was read accordingly.'

Way| Mr. Fane, according to Order, reported, from the and Means. Committee of the whole House, to whom it was referred to consider further of Ways and Means for raising the Supply granted to his Majesty, the Resolution which the Committee had directed him to report to the House; which he read in his Place; and afterwards delivered in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

Resolved, That it is the Opinion of this Committee, -That, towards railing the Supply granted to his Majesty, the Sum of Six millionsThree hundred thousand Pounds be raised by transferrable Annuities, after the Rate of Four Pounds per Centum per Annum;and that an additional

Capital of Ten Pounds be added to every One hundred Pounds advanced; the said additional Capital to be by way of Lottery, consisting of Tickets of the Value of Ten Pounds each, the Blanks and Prizes to bear an Interest of Four Pounds per Centum per Annumthe Interest of the said Annuities and Lottery to commence from Michaelmas 1748: That every Subscriber shall, on or before the 12th Diy of December instant, make a Deposit of Ten Pounds peeCeutiak mth the-Cashiers of the Bank of ' England; and every Subscriber paying in the Whole, or any Part , of his Money, at or before the Time, or respective Times, that shall be appointed for the Payment thereof, such Subscriber shall be allowed Interest after the Rftc of Five Pounds per Centum per to be

computed from the Day on which such actual Payment shall have been made, to Michaelmas next; and that the said Deposit, and all other Sums paid to the Cashiers of the Bank, in virtue of this Resolution, shall by them be paid into the Receipt of his Majesty's Exchequer, to be applied from time to time to such Services as shall then have been voted by this House in this Session of Parliament. and not otherwise.

The said Resolution, being read a Second time, was, upon the Question put thereupon, agreed to by the House.

Foreign The House being informed. That the Sheriffs of the Protostants City of London attended at the Door 1

And the said Petition was read j setting forth, That the Petitioners having observfed, by the Votes of this House, that a Bill hath been brought in for a general Naturalization of foreign Protestants, think it their indif-penfable Duty to represent the Mischiefs that they apprehend will flow from this Bill, if passed into a Law; and that the Petitioners, as Citizens of , will be

particularly affected by such a Law, by the Decrease, if

Vol. 25.

500,000 ——

not total Loss, of the Duties of Package, Scavage, Portage, and Balliage, of the Goods of foreign Merchants, granted by many Royal Charters, and confirmed by several Acts of Parliament: And further expressing the Apprehensions of the Petitioners, that the Naturalization of all foreign Protestants, indiscriminately, is more Jikejy to increase the Poverty, than make any Addition to the Wealth of this Nation s for that neither the Rich nor the Industrious amongst them need any such Inducement, as the latter never want Encouragement, nor the former the very Privilege in question, when they apply to Parliament for it: And representing to the House, That a like Law being attempted in the Reign of the late King Wi/liamt it was rejected on such national Considerations, as, it is presumed, can never escape the Attention, nor lose the Regard, of this House; and the Experiment being made, by passing a Law for that Purpose, in the Reign of the late Queen Anne, it was found so detrimental to the publick Interest, that it was shortly after repealed, and not without some Rcfledions on the Mischiefs it had produced; and that as Naturalization cannot convey to Foreigners a true Knowledge of our happy Constitution in Church and State, or give them such Zeal and Affection for it, as may be requisite for maintaining and defending it, and as those who have grown up under arbitrary Government, may be fitted to an fiver arbitrary Purposes, too much Caution cannot be used in a Matter erf" such great Importance: And therefore praying, That the said Bill may not pass into a Law.

Ordered, That the said Petition do lie upon the Table.

The Lord Dupplin, according to Order, reported, from the Committee of Privileges and Elections, the Matter, as it appeared to them, touching the Election for the Borough of Withyotherwise Droilwich, in the County of

Worcester; together with the Resolutions of the Committee thereupon; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: YVhere the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

Upon the Petition of the Honourable Edwin Sandy*,

6 Esquire,

DroitKrich

Election.

Droitwich

Election.

470 16* Decembris. A. 1747.

Esquire, complaining of an undue Election and Return of Thomas Foley the younger, Esquire, to serve in this present Parliament for the Borough of otherwise Droitwich, in the County of Worcester.

The Committee have examined the Merits of this Election.

And the last Determination of the House, concerning the Right of Election of Burgesses to l'erve in Parliament for the said Borough, made the 11 th Day of November 1690 (when it was resolved, That the Right of electing Burgesses to serve in Parliament for the Borough of Droitwich, is in the Burgesses of the Corporation of the Salt Springs of Droitwich) being read, as also the (landing Order of the House, made the 16th Day of January 1735, for restraining Counsel at the Bar of the House of Commons, or before the Committee of Elections, from offering Evidence touching the Legality of Votes for Members to serve in Parliament, contrary to the lad Determination of the House;

The Counsel for the Petitioner alleged, That Droitwich is a Borough by Prescription: That there are ancient Salt Springs belonging thereto, called the Corporation Springs, in Contradiftindlion to other Salt Springs since discovered, there, or thereabouts: That all the Burgesses of the said Borough claim their Right of Burgesship by Election, or Primogeniture; but they infilled that, according to the said Resolution of the House, neither Election nor Primogeniture can qualify a Burgess to vote at any Election of Members to serve in Parliament, unless he has a Share or Property in the said ancient Salt Springs.

At the same time they declared, That they would not impeach the Right of any Burgess, for Want of such Property, who hath constantly acted as a Burgess, and been reputed such, for above Twenty Years.

Then having produced the original Poll, taken at the last Election, wherein the Numbers appear to be,

For the Sitting Member, Thomas Foley the younger, Esquire - - - - 19

For the Petitioner, the Honourable Edwin Sandys Esquire - - - 18

They objected to Nine of the Voters for the Sitting Member; viz.

To Four, elected Burgesses in the Year 1741, as not having Property in the said ancient Springs.

To other Four, who claim by Primogeniture, as not having such Property.

To One, as not being either elected a Burgess, or the eldell Son of a Burgess, or possessed of any such Property as aforesaid.

And they called Mr. John Ingram, formerly Town-Clerk of the said Borough: Who said, That he was present at the last Election at when the Four

Persons following, viz.John JolliJfe Esquire, Humphrey Lowe Esquire, Rowland Berkeley Esquire, and Robert Harley Esquire, gave their Votes; and Objections being severally made to their Right of Voting, upon Account of their not having Property in the ancient Salt Springs, Mr. Jolliffeowned that he had not any; and the other

Three declined giving any Answer to that Point; but they all infilled to vote, as having been eladled and sworn Burgesses; and Three of them alleged, that they had served the Office of Bailiff.

Upon Cross-Examination, he owned; That he heard Mr. Lowe (One of the Four) declare, that he believed he had a Property in the Salt Springs; and that the Conveyance of it was in the Hands of Mr. Roger the

present Town-Clerk of Droitwich.

Being further cross-examined, he said, That he apprehends no Person can be elected a Burgess, or is capable of serving the Offices of the Corporation, who has not Property in the Salt Springs: That the Four Gentlemen objected to have each of them served the Office of Bailiff; and that there may be other Instances of Persons having served the said Office, who had not Property; for he believes, that, of late. Property has not been regarded; as there hath not been, in his Memory, any

Controversy concerning Elections of Corporation Officers, till Michaelmas 1745, nor any Conteftat the Election of Members to serve in Parliament, except the last Election.

He said further, That the ancient Springs having been many Years dried up, and no visible Enjoyment of the Property, it cannot be known who has or has not Property in them, otherways than by Title Deeds.

Then the said Mr. Ingram being examined,«as to what passed at the Time of the Election, with relation to the Four other Persons, claiming as elded Sons of Burgesses, and objected to as not having Property in the Salt Springs, said, That this Objection was made at the Tirtie of the Election, to the Four Persons following; viz. John -ington Esquire, Mr. Other Philpot, John Talbot junior, Esquire, and Thomas Foley junior, Esquire, the Sitting Member; none of whom pretended that they had any such Property; and the Two Gentlemen last named claimed expressly to vote, as being eldell Sons of Burgesses.

When he was crots-examineci to this Point of Objection, he said. That the eldell Sons of Burgesses have been admitted to act as Burgesses in the Life-time of their Fathers; and that, from the Reputation of the Place, he always understood they had acied in Right of their being eldell Sons: That, till the last Election, he never knew any Objection made to them, on account of their Want of Property in the Salt Springs.

That there are in the Town Books, as far as they go back, several Instances, where Persons, claiming as eldest Sons, have acted as Burgesses in the Life-time of their Fathers, and have voted in Elections of Corporation Officers, feme of whom have exercised the Office of Bailiff'; but whether those Persons had or had not Property in the Salt Springs, the Witness could give no Account.

He further laid, That he was inclined to believe that the late Mr. Thomas Winnington, who in the Year 1722 acted as Burgess in the Life-time of his Father, had not then such Property; nor does he believe that Mr. Francis Winnington, One of the present Sitting Members for this Borough, had such Property, when he acted as Burgess in his Father's Life-time.

With respect to the Objection made to Andrew Wind-for Esquire, as not being either elected a Burgess, or the eldell Son of a Burgess, or intitled to any Properly in' the Salt Springs;

The said Mr. Ingram being examined, said. That he was chosen Town-Clerk of Droitzvich in the Year 17221 That no Entry appears in the Corporation Books to shew that Mr. Windsor was ever ekdled a Burgess: That he is the youngest Son of the Lord Windsor, who was afterwards Earl of Plymouth, and is about 70 or 80 Years of Age.

That by the Usage of the Borough, no younger Son of a Burgess can claim a Right to be a Burgess, unless the eldell Son dies without Issue.

Being cross-examined, he laid. That he hath inspected the Town-Books, as far back as the Year 1677; and that Mr. Windsor appears to havesigned an Entry therein,

as a Burgess, once; viz. in the Year 1721, upon an Election of Corporation Officers.

The Counsel for the Sitting Member admitted. That Property in the ancient Salt Springs is a neceflSry Qualification of an elected Burgess; but not of a Burgeli claiming by Primogeniture; and infilled. That nothing appears upon the Face of the last Resolution of the House to determine the Qualification of a Burgess; and that whoever has a Right to act as a Butgefs, is intitled to vote in the Election of Members to serve in Parliament.

That the eldell Son of a Burgess is, ipso faHo, a B urgefs, and may, when of Age, exercise all the Rights of Bur-

Eefsship, without any other Qualification: And they ob-:rved the Evidence, produced by the Petitioner's Counsel, declared this to have been the Usage.

Being cross-examined, he said. He could not be certain whether those Persons, who claimed by Right of Primogeniture, and whom he remembers to have acted as Burgesses and Bailiffs in the Life-time of their Fathers, had or had not Property in the Salt Springs; but that be never heard they had any.

Mr. Henry Roberts, aged 50 Years, said, That he has lived at Droitwich all his Life-time, except Five Years, but is no Burgess: That the cldcft Sons of Burgesses were always deemed to have a Right to vote, while their Fathers were living; and that several have voted incorporation Elections, in virtue of such Right, without any other Qualification.

Translation of his Britannick Majesty's Act of Consent to the Convention between the States General and his Swedish Majesty, Landgrave of HeJJe, for 3,040 Men: Hague, 9 June 1747.

Their High MightineSTcs being about to treat, and ready to conclude, a Convention with his Majesty, Landgrave of Hesse, for a Body of 3,040 Men, which is to enter into the Service and Pay of the Repub-lick; and the Republick being to engage herfeif, in order to defray the Expences which the Entertainment of the said Troops shall cause his Swedish Majesty, to pay an annual Subsidy of Seventy-five thousand Banco Rix dollars during the Two Years that they shall be actually in the Pay of the Republick; and an Augmentation of that Subsidy, at the Rate of One hundred and Twenty-five thousand Banco Rix-dollars, valued at 53 Stivers current Money of Holland, for the Time that they shall be no more in the Pay of the Republick, and that they shall be fentback: His Britannick Majesty engages himself, by this present Act, to contribute to the said Subsidies the Three-fourths upon the Foot of the Agreement made in the Article of the Refultat, of the 9th January 1747,

N. S. with respect to the extraordinary Expences of the War, and the new or farther Subsidies which shall be thought fit to be promised to some Courts or Princes, without his said Majesty's charging himself with any future Expence for the ordinary Entertainment of the Said Troops.

And whereas his Swedish Majesty is engaged to his Britannick Majesty, to hold his Troops ready for the Service of his said Majesty, in case he Should have Occasion for their Service, without being at Liberty to give them to others but with his Leave; his Britannick Majesty, to Shew his Friendship for his good and faithful Allies the States General, and his Zeal for the Good of the common Cause, consents and permits, that the said Body of 3,040 Men may enter into the Service of the Republick in the manner expressed by the Treaty projected between his Swedish Majesty and their High MightineSTcs the 3d June 1747.

Done at the Hague the 9th June 1747.

Signed

(L. S.) SANDWICH.

Translation of the Extract out of the Register of the Resolutions of the High and Mighty Lords, the States General of the United Provinces.

Wednesday, 5 July 1747.

After Deliberation upon what the Earl of Sandwich, Minister Plenipotentiary from his Majesty the King of Great Britain, represented on the 9th June last, in a

Conference to the Deputies of their High Mightinesse for foreign Affairs, viz. That his said Majesty having givem Orders to the Earl of Hyndford, to conclude and sign a Treaty with her Majesty the Empress of all the Jias, by virtue of which her laid Imperial Majesty is obliged, during One Year, to be computed from the Day of the signing the said Treaty, to hold in Readiness, upon the Frontiers of Livonia, bordering upon Lithuania, a Body of Thirty thousand Men, Infantry, of her national Troops, exclusive of between Forty and Fifty Gallies upon those Coasts, properly equipped, so that they may be in a Condition to act, upon the first Requisition which his tannick Majesty shall make, and in such Places where it shall be necessary to assist his said Majesty, and his Allies: And that his said Majesty, in order to contribute, on his Part, towards the Expences which the Maintenance of the said Troops and Gallies cause to her Imperial Majesty, being to engage to furnifti her, once for ail, for this Year, One hundred thousand Pounds Sterling, as soon as the Ratifications of the said Treaty shall be exchanged; he did not in the least doubt. That their High Mighti-nesses, finding this Project so advantageous for the common Cause, would consent to pay their Contingent in the said Subsidy, upon the Foot of the Agreement made in the Article of the RefuUat, of the 9 January last, N. S. concerning the extraordinary Expences of the War; It has been found good, and resolved. That the said Earl of Sandwich shall be answered upon the said P.oposition, That their High Mightinesse apprehend, with his said Majesty, that the said projected Treaty will tend to the great Advantage of the common Cause; and that therefore they are dii posed and ready to contribute One-fourth, for their Contingent in the Subsidy of £. ioom Sterling promised by that Treaty for One Year, upon the Foot of the Agreement made in the Article of the of

9 January last, concerning the extraordinary Charges of the War; and the new or ulterior Sulidies, which shall be judged necessary to be allowed to some Courts or Princes, without their charging themselves thereby with any farther Expences, for the ordinary Entertainment of the said Troops.

And, for that Purpose, an Act or Declaration shall be drawn up in Writing, which shall be given to the said Earl of Sandwich, or, in his Absence, to the Resident Mr. Dayrolle.

Translation of the States General's Act of Consent to the Treaty of Subsidy, concluded with 5

July 1747, N. S.

His Majesty the King of Great Britain, being about to treat, and ready to conclude, a Treaty with her Majesty the Empress of all the RuJJias, in consequence of which Treaty, her said Imperial Majesty, during the Term of One Year, to be computed from the Day of the Signature of the said Treaty, is to hold in Readiness, upon the Frontiers of Livonia, bordering upon Lithuania, a Body of 30" Men, Infantry, of her national Troops, exclusive of between 40 and 50 Gallies, with the necessary Equipages, upon those Coasts, in a Manner that that Body may aft upon the first Requisition to be made by his said Britannick Majesty, and in such Place wh^re Necessity may require it to assist his said Majesty, and his Allies; and his Britannick Majesty being to engage,

in order to contribute towards the Expences which the Entertainment of the said Troops and Gallies will cause to her said Imperial Majesty, to pay, once for all, for this Year, a Subsidy of f. 100'" Sterling, as soon as the Ratifications of the said Treaty shall be exchanged; their High Mightinesse engage themselves, by this present Act, to contribute to the said Subsidy One-fourth, upon the Foot of the Agreement made in the Refultat, of the 9th January 1747, N.S. with regard to the extraordinary Expences of the War, and the new or ulterior Subsidies, which shall be thought proper to be promised to some Courts or Princes, without their High Mightinesse charging themselves with any farther Expence lor the ordinary Entertainment of the said Troops.

In Witness whereof. We have caused the present Act to be signed by the President of our Assembly, and to be subscribed by our First Grefiier.

Signed,

Hague, 5 July 1 747. C. Beni inch.

(L. S.) Subscribed,

By Command of the States General,

H. Fagel.

Sir Hugh Smithson reported from the Committee, to whom the Petition of the Justices of the Peace, Gentlemen, Freeholders, and Inhabitants, of the County of Durham, whose Names are thereunto subsetibed, was Vol. 25.

referred; That the Committee had examined the Matter of the said' Petition; and had directed him to report the lame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place, and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition,

In the Name of the Holy and Undivided Trinity.

Whereas his Majesty the King of Britain, and her Imperial Majesty of ali the Ruffas, have mutually engaged, by the Treaty of defendve Alliance concluded in the Year One thousand Seven hundred Forty-two, and which Hill subsists so happily between the Two high Parties to employ their particular Care to preserve the general Tranquillity of Europe, and to extend farther their Engagements of Friendship as Occasion shall require; and that her Imperial Majesty of all the Ruffins has, on her Part, very much lamented the Peace and Tranquillity being disturbed for some Years pad in Europe, and the Re-establishment of which upon the ancient Footing, is, according to all Appearance, not only far off, but that also the present Danger even increases, by the Superiority of the Forces of the Enemies of her high Allies; and that, for this Reason, flie has only waited for a favourable Opportunity to remedy it; and as his Majesty the King of Great Britain has communicated, in Confidence to her Imperial Majesty of all the Rnffias, by the Earl of ford, his Ambassador extraordinary' and Plenipotentiary, redding at this Court, his Intention, to wit, That his Majesty, in order to advance this Re-establishment so dedred, and to obtain the common Quiet and Balance in Europe, and consequently to attain this filutary Dedgn, tending to put an End to the Troubles of Europe, would be willing, jointly with their high Mightinesse the Lords the States General of the United Provinces of the Low Countries, to take of her Imperial Majesty of all the RuJJias to his Assistance, and into his Service, as well as that of his other Allies, a Body of Thirty thousand Men of her Troops, on Condition of certain Subddics which shall be agreed upon on the one Part and the other; and that thefr High Mightmeffes have likewise made known to her

Article II.

As the said Body of Auxiliary Imperial Troops of Ruffin, to be yielded, is already upon the Frontiers of Livonia, in a Condition to march, it shall be put in Motion Vol. 25.

from the said Frontiers of Livonia as soon as possible, after Convention the Exchange of the Ratifications of the present Conven- w'th Holhnd, tion, and shall set out from Cottrland in the Month of c* January of the next Year One thousand Seven hundred Forty-eight, continuing its Rout towards the Rhine, in order to be there employed in Conjunction with the other Troops of the Allies, either upon the Moselle, or in the L<nv Countries, as the Occasion of War shall require. Article III.

The said Body of Auxiliary'Troops shall lie maintained and provided with Portions and Rations and other Necessaries, at the Expence of her Imperial Majesty of all the RuJJias, during its March from the Frontiers of Russia, through Poland, to the Frontiers of Upper Silesia; in Confederation of which, his Majesty the King of Great Britain, and their High Mightinesse, oblige themselves to pay her Imperial Majesty of all the RuJJias, at Riga, and before-hand, in ready Money, immediately after the Exchange of the Ratifications of the present Convention, and independently' of the Subsidies of Three hundred thousand Pounds Sterling, stipulated above, but apart, the Sum of One hundred Fifty thousand Crowns of to be employed in making the necessary Provisions far this March. When this Body of Auxiliary- Troops shall be arrived on the Frontiers of Upper Silesia, to wit, at the Town of Bilitz, the Commissaries, who shall be ex-prdsly appointed for that Purpose, on the Part of his Majesty the King of Great Britain, as also of their High Mightinesse, shall receive it, and charge themselves with its Maintenance, at their own Expencej and the said Commissaries shall cause to be delivered to it, not only upon its farther March from the said Town of Bilitz, but also during all the Time that the said Body shall remain in the Service of the Two Maritime Powers, and till it be returned upon the Frontiers of Poland, the Portions and Rations inNaturd-, to wit, to the Non-commissioned Officers, Soldiers, and others, in Portions, each Man a Day, Two Pounds of Rye Bread, One Pound of Meat, or Fish on Fast-Days, or else the Value of a £ound of Meat in Money, One Quarter of a Pound of Oatmeal, as also Two Pounds of Sait a Month; and in Rations, for each Horse a Day, Six Pounds Two-thirds of Oats, Sixteen Pounds Tyro-thirds of Hay, and besides chopped Straw, upon the same Foot as is given to their own Horses, and those of the other Allied Troops; the whole in Holland Weight. At the Approach of the Time of Winter Quarters, convenient Quarters shall be assigned to all the said Auxiliary Troops, without excepting the Generality, nor the Officers as well of the great as of the small Staff1; and shall furnish them Wood and other Necessaries without Payment. In case of Mortality of any of the Bag-gage-Horses, during the March of the said Body, and before it reaches the Frontiers of Upper ,the Maritime Powers engage, besides, to supply their own Voor Spann, for the said Deficiency of Horses, from the said Frontiers of Upper Silesia, without deducting the Colts either from the Total of the stipulated Subsidies, or from the Money which, as has been laid above, shall be paid for the Provisions.

For the rest, the Subsistence of the said Troops shall be constantly paid them on the Part of her Imperial Majesty of all the Ruffias.

Article IV.

These Auxiliary Troops being arrived at the Place appointed upon the Rhine, they shall, as has been said above, be employed there, as well as any-where else where the Occasion of War Hull require, and where the Maritime Powers, with their Allies, shall find it proper; on Condition, neverthelds, that, although this Body of Thirty thousand Men be granted to the Two Maritime Powers jointly, it shall, however, be never separated, either upon the March in going thither or in returning, or in case of Counter-marches, Operations, and Actions; but that it shall be kept together as much as possible, and that it shall act in Conjunction with the Troops of the Maritime Powers and the other Allies,

Article V.

These Auxiliary Troops shall be commanded by the Imperial General of Russia that Hull be at their Head; who shall lolely depend on the Person who shall have the Command as well of the Troops of the Maritime Powers, as of those of their other Allies upon the Rhine, or upon the Moselle, or in the Low Countries, or to the Person on whom the Command shall devolve, during his Absence; and shall receive from him only the Word and Orders: For the rest, no important Enterprize shall be undertaken, without having previously deliberated upon, and formed the Resolutioa in, a Council of War, and in Presence of the Commanding Imperial General of Russia.

Article VI.

These Auxiliary Troops shall have their own Priests, and the free Exercise of their Religion; and shall conduct themselves in whatever relates to the military Service accord inglp their own Imperial Russian Regulations, Articles, ana military Constitutions: But if any Disputes. shall happen between the Officers or Soldiers of the combined Troops, they shall be examined and decided by an equal Number of respective Commissaries of both Parties, and the Offenders shall be pur.ished each according to the military Laws of their Sovereign. It shall likewise be lawful for the Generals and other Persons of these Auxiliary Troops, during the whole Time they shall be in the Service of the Maritime Powers, to carry on a free Correspondence with their Country, without any Hindrance, either by Letters or by Expresses, and as often as they shall please.

Article VII.

notwithstanding that by the Fourth Article it is a) ready expressly agreed, that this Body of Auxiliary Troops

shall be kept together as much as can be, and that it shall not be divided, it is farther reserved, in particular, that these Troops shall not be exposed to greater Fatigues than the others; and that for this Reason a perfect Equality shall be observed in all Expeditions and Operations: The Commander in chief therefore shall be obliged to observe a just Proportion in all Detachments which shall be nude according to the State and Force of the whole Army. It is farther agreed amongst the high contracting Parties, that these Auxiliary Troops shall enjoy, in the Enemy's Countries and Places wheresoever they may be, in general, and without any Exception, the func Plunder as the Maritime Powers shall allow their own Troops to enjoy: The same Thing is understood also with regard to Trophies, as Cannon, Colours, and other Things, which shall have been taken by the said Auxiliary Troops from the Enemy, on Occasion of an Action, and which consequently shall remain their Spoil.

Article VIII.

The said Auxiliary Body shall be provided on the Part of Russia with whatever it shall want in Clothes, Arms, and other necessary Munitions, during the First Year, to be reckoned from its March; but whatever shall be judged necessary to be Cent to the said Body, after the Expiration of that Year, flvill be transported and delivered from the Frontiers of Russia, at the Expence of the Maritime Powers; And as far the rest, feme of these Things which the Regiments may want, cannot be replaced, by rcalon of the Distance from the Frontiers of they shall be

all delivered to the said Imperial Russian Body, rn the Part ofrhe Maritime Powers and of their Allies, from the Countries where they shall be had, at a reasonable Price.

Article IX.

As for Powder and Ball, they shall be supplied on the Part of Russia, as well for the Soldiers as for the Field-pieces of the Regiments, as also whatever is requilitcfor the said Field-pieces, in as great a Quantity as is customary on Marches, the whole being lent all at once, with the Auxiliary Troops; but in case of a longer Halt of the said Troops in those Countries, they shall be provided with all those Things, without paying, on the Part of the Maritime Powers, or of the other Allies, to be made use of in the Operations against the Enemy.

Article X.

notwithstanding that this Body shall have, asusual, its own Surgeons, with their Mates, and the necessary Drugs to cure their Sick, with each Regiment, it is, however, agreed, that in case the said Auxiliary1Troops should be put in Motion, or employed in military Operations against the Enemies of the Maritime Powers, or of their Allies, not being able, for that llcafon, to have and take care of the Sick and Wounded with their Regiments, on account of their great and dangerous Illnesses, and that they should be obliged to leave them behind in any neighbouring Towns or Villages, that then they shall always not only be received by Conimiffiaries, expressly to be appointed for that Purpose, on the Part of the above-mentioned Maritime Powers, but that the said Sick and Wounded shall be also taken care of in a convenient and necessary Place, and provided with their own Surgeons and Medicines: They iliali be also supported equally at their own Expence, and further fub-fifted in every thing, on the fume Footing as is ordinarily practised in the Hospitals, with respect to the People of the Maritime Powers own Troops, and of the other Allies: The Persons whom it shall be indispensably necessary to leave of the above-mentioned Auxiliary Troops with those Sick, to serve and take care of them, shall likewise be provided with Quarters, and fubfilted at the Expence of the Maritime Powers, on the same Footing as has been above llipulated, with regard to thelc Auxiliary Troops. likewise, if, on the Return of thele Auxiliary Troops to Russia, they should be obliged to leave any Sick behind for some Time, and People with them to take care of them, the Maritime Powers charge themselves in general with their Entertainment and Subsistence, at their own Expence; and shall cause theni all to be transported and elcorted to Russia, either by Land or by Sea, as can

be most conveniently done, after the Sick shall be recovered: All the Money laid out for the Entertainment and Transportat ion, as well of those Sick as of the military Persons of the Imperial Troops of Russia, who shall be with them, to take care of them, shall in no-wife be deduced from the Sum of the Subsidies to be paid.

Article XI.

In case that, on account of the Operations of the War, any of these Auxiliary Imperial Troops of should be made Prisoners by the Enemy, they shall not be left in such same without Care being taken for their Liberty; but the Maritime Powers promise on their Side to use their utrnoft Effort chat they may be ransomed immediately, or after the Armidice, as Opportunity shall offer, at the Expence of the Lid Maritime Powers; or that they be releated by virtue of the Cartel which should then subsist between the Two belligerent Parties, and be returned to flic said Auxiliary Troops. In Return, all the Prisoners who shall be taken by the said Body of Auxiliary Troops from the Enemy, shall be delivered up to the General Commander in Chief of the Allied Troops, except the Ddcrters of these Auxiliary Troops, Subje&s of in case there shall be any amongst those Prisoners.

Article XII.

His Majesty the King of Gr , and their High Mightinesses, promise, by virtue of the present Article, to use their Endeavours, to the end that it be most rigorously prohibited in the States of her Majesty the Empress of the Ramans, Queen of Hungary and and of

their other Allies, to receive any-where any Deserter of these Auxiliary Troops, nor to engage them in any Service; and dill lei's to retain any one under other Pretences, but to cause the Deserters to be seized, where-ever they shall be found, and to fend them forthwith, without Exception or Excul'e, to the General Commander of the said Troops: On the other hand, the General Commander of this Auxiliary Imperial Corps of shall be obliged to give up to the General Commander in Chief of the Troops of the Maritime Powers, and of their other Allies, all the Deserters who should take Refuge with this Auxiliary Corps of Russia, of whatsoever Nation they may be, excepting the Subje&s of her Imperial Majesty of all the Raffias.

Article XIII.

Notwithstanding it be laid in the Fird Article, that this Auxiliary Body of Imperial Russian Troops is yielded to the Disposal of the Maritime Powers, for Two Years, to be computed from the Day which they shall march from the Frontiers, it is nevertheless agreed, that in case Peace be made with the Maritime Powers, before the Expiration of the said Term, or that they should not have farther Occasion for them, the said Troops shall be lent back into the Empire of Russia sooner, and even before the Term of Two Years.

But in case that the Peace be not made, and that these Auxiliary Troops be retained in the Service of the Maritime Powers above Two Years, they shall declare it in Time, to wit, Four Months before the Expiration of the Term, to the end, that they may agree anew about the longer Stay of the said Troops in those Countries. In like manner, when it shall be found necefliuy, on the Part of Russia, not to leave this Auxiliary Body above the Time ol Two Years in the Service of the Maritime Powers, but to make them indispensably return. Notice shall be also given to the said Maritime Powers, Four Month? before the Expiration of the Term: A* for the red, it is also agreed, that if it happens there be no farther Occasion fur these Troops to lie employed there in the Service, then they shall not, however, be tint back into Russia, but in a convenient Season (or the March; the Autumn and Winter Months, therefore, a> those of ber, November, December, January, and February, shall be expressly and namely excepted out ol thete Marches.

Article XIV.

If the Empire of Russia, alter the fending of the said Troops, fr.ould be attacked by any Chridian Power, in that Cafe, the Marit.me Powers promise and engage not only to fend back these Auxiliary Troops immediately

Article XVI.

In case that one or the other of these Two Maritime Powers should not be longer inclined to keep the said Body of Auxiliary Troops, or that it should judge proper, on account of some Circumstances, of whatsoever Nature they may be, and which could not be foreseen, to depart from the Engagements taken on this Head, the said Maritime Powers bind themselves not only to answer the One for the other, and to keep alone this Body as long as they should have Occasion, but to pay also readily, and without Hesitation, the Subsidies dipulated for this Body; Co that in case his Majesty the King of Great Britain departs, contrary to all Expectation, in ooe way or another, from his Engagements, then the Republick of the United Provinces of the Low Countries shall be obliged, nevertheless, to fulfil alone the Conditions dipulated by this Convention, to keep this Body intire together, and to pay the whole Sum of the Subsidies which is agreed on: The like Performance is likewise to be understood, vice versa, on the Part of his Majesty the King of Great Britain, to wit. That in case the Lords the States General of the United Provinces of the Low Countries do not execute the Conditions dipulated, then his Majesty the King of Great Britain binds himself in like manner to fulfil alone the Conditions dipulated by this Convention, to keep this whole Body, and to pay the whole Sum of the Subsidy which is agreed on.

Proposals for furnishing a Body of the Troops of Hanover, to be employed in the Low Countries, for the Service of the Year 1748.

Whereas a Body of his Majesty's Electoral Troops, confiding of Five thousand Horse, and Thirteen thousand Foot, were taken into the Pay of Great Britain, to act in the Low Countries, with the Austrian Troops and those of the States General of the United Provinces, until the 25th Day of November 1747: And whereas it was judged necessary for the publick Service, that our Orders should be sent, in the Month of July last, for the immediate March of Five additional Regiments of our said Electoral Troops, confiding of Four thousand and Seventy Foot, with the necessary Train of Artillery, to reinforce the Body ot Troops in the Pay of Great Britain, in Conjunction with the Army of his Majesty's Allies in and the said Regiments did accordingly immediately begin their March, and actually join the said Army: And whereas it is found necessary that the said Body of Troops, together with the said Five additional P.egiments, should be continued for the Year 1748, towards completing the Number of Men which Great Britain is to maintain in the Low Countries, to act as aforesaid; his Majesty, in Confederation of the great Difficulties in obtaining such a Number of Men for this Purpose, pro-poles to continue the said Five thousand Horse, and Thirteen thousand Foot, together with the said additional Number of Four thousand and Seventy Foot, amounting in the whole to Twenty-two thousand and Seventy Men, to act in the Low Countries for the Year 1748, on th following Conditions: That is to say.

That there be granted to his Majesty, for defraying the Expence of the Pay and Subsistence of the said Body of Troops, to consist of Five thousand Horse, and Seventeen

That he was particularly acquainted with the Works which were begun in the Year 1743, and have been since carried on for that Purpose:

Which Works consist of a Fire Engine, Two Refer-voirs to supply the said Engine, and Two other, from whence the Water is conveyed by Pipes to the several Houses in the Parishes aforesaid:

That upwards of £. 5,000 has already been expended in the said Undertaking, which is far from complete; and that he apprehends £. 6,000 more must be laid out to bring the Work to such Perfection as to supply the Inhabitants of the adjacent Parts, who are feme of them obliged to be supplied by Carts at a very great Expence.

A Petition of the Mayor, Bailiffs, and Burgesses, of the Borough and Corporation of Liverpool, in the County of Lancaster, and of the Inhabitants and Parishioners thereof, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That, by an Act of Parliament, made in the Tenth and Eleventh Years of the Reign of the late King William the Third, the Town of Uverpool aforesaid, on account of its great Trade, and being also very populous, was made a Parish of itself, distinct from the Parish of Walton, in the said County; and the Inhabitants of Liverpool aforesaid were thereby empowered, at their own Charge, to build a Church within the said Town, and endow the fame, as therein directed; and that, by an Act of Parliament, made in the First Year of the Reign of his late Majesty King George the First, the said Mayor, Bailiffs, and Burgesses, on account of the great Increase of Tradeand People, of and within the said Town, fine; the Building of the said Church, were impowered to build another Church or Chapel, at their own Charge, on the Site of the late Castle within the said Town, and to have a Curate or Chaplain, being a Minister of the Church of Vql. 25.

England, as by Law established, to officiate and perform Divine Service therein; and at their own Charge to endow the same Church; which Two said Churches have been long since perfeded and endowed; and that Divine Service hath been ever since duly performed therein; and that the Powers of the said several Acts have been faithfully executed: And further setting forth. That, since the Building of the said last Church or Chapel, the said Town is greatly increased in Trade, and its Inhabitants, proses-sing the Doctrine of the Church of England, are become much more numerous than heretofore; and that it is daily increasing in People, Trade, and Buildings; lb that both the said Churches, and the parochial Chapel of Our Lady and St. Nicholas, long before erected, and since very much enlarged, at the Expence and Charge of the said Corporation, are not all together capable of containing One Half of the Inhabitants of the said Parish, professing the Doctrine of the Church of; and that there is

now great Necessity for the Building of more Churches or Chapels within the said Town, and to have more Mi-nifters of the Church of England to officiate and perform Divine Service therein, in order that many of the Inhabitants of Liverpool, professing the Doctrine of the Church of England, may be fitted and supplied with Seats or Pews for performing Divine Worship therein, which they now cannot have in the present Churches or Chapels; and that, for the effecting so good a Design, many of the Parishioners of the said Parish have already subscribed a sufficient Sum of Money for the Building and Endowing ot a Church on the South Side of the Town, upon Ground given by Mr. fo/ni OkiU Merchant, and Company, which they hold by Lease for Three Lives, and Twenty-one Years, under the Corporation; and that the said Corporation have agreed to give their rwerlionary Right and Interest therein, for the Purpose aforesaid: And representing to the House, That the Town of Liverpool, being now become a Place of great Extent, and very numerous in its Buildings and Inhabitants, there is now great Necessity to have publick Scavengers within the said Town, for clean sing the Streets, and also to have the Streets enlightened with Lamps, and a regular and able Watch to be conllantly kept in the Night-time throughout the said Town, in like manner as in several great Towns in this Kingdom is uled, for the Conveni-ency and Benefit of the Inhabitants, and for the Safety of their Persons, Houses, and Effects; the Expence of doing which cannot be provided for and supported by the customary Laws and Rules of the said Borough and Corporation of Liverpool-, and that the said Petitioners have, at a publick Meeting of Vestry, upon due Notice given held within the said Town for that Purpose, unanimously consented to lay a Tax upon themselves, to defray the Expence thereof: And therefore praying. That the Committee had examined the Matter of t he said Petition; and had directed him to report the fame, as it appeared to them, to the House; and he read the Report in his Place; and afterwards delivered it in at the Clerk's Table: Where the same was read; and is as followeth; viz.

To prove the Allegations of the said Petition,

John Brice was examined: Who said, That he hath known the Lands described in the Petition (containing about 7,000 Acres) Thirty Years: That formerly they produced good Crops of Oats, and other Grain; but that, of late, they are of little or no Value, by reaion of their being often overflowed; and particularly, that as they are at this Time Two Feet under Water, occasioned from the Outfalls to the Sea being greatly impaired, and by the Banks of the several Drains being low, and for the Want of Mills to drain off the Water.

Daniel Adcock, being examined, said, That the said Lands are often overflowed; but that, by railing the Banks, and keeping them in Repair, and, by erecting Mills for draining off the Water, these Lands would produce Five Quarters of Oats, or Big Barley, per Acre.

Ordered, That Leave be given to bring in a Bill for draining and prelesving certain Fen Lands, in the several Parishes of Money, UpwWelney, Witch-

ford, and Wentworth, and in a certain extra-parochial Place called Byall Fen, in the Isle of Ely and County of Cambridge: And that Mr. Fellowes and Mr. Compton do prepare, and bring in, the fame.

Examining A Petition of several Persons, whose Names are there-Prugfc &c. unto subscribed. Apothecaries of the Cities of London and

Westminster, on behalf of themselves, and all other the regular Apothecaries of the said Cities and Suburbs thereof, was presented to the House, and read; setting forth, That the Apothecaries of London, being formerly incorporated with the Grocers, or dispersed amongst the other Companies of the said City, without any Regulation or Form of Government amongst themselves, with regard to the Business of preparing Medicines; and such Defect .20

being found productive of many Inconveniences and Mif-chiefsto the Publick, for Remedy thereof King James the First, by the Advice of his Physicians, did, by his Letters Patent, bearing Date the Sixth Day of December, in the 15th Year of his Reign, form the said Apothecaries into adiftinct Society, by the Name of the Mailer, Wardens, and Society, of the Art and Mystery of Apothecaries of the City of Lonwith Power and Authority to search for anddestroy all deceitful, fta!e, corrupt, unmedicinable, and pernicious Daigsand Medicines; and to examine and suppiefsall ignorant, unskilful, and ungovernable Practices; which Authority was by the said Letters Patent, declared to extend over all Persons whatever, that should prepare or fell any Drugs or Medicines within the said City of London, and Seven Miles thereof; and that the Jurisdiction of the said Society, being nevertheless, in later Times, understood to affect only their own Members, it is become, in a great measure, impossible for them to anliver the publick and filutary Ends of their Incorporation, without the Aid and Interposition of Parliament; and that several ignorant, unlkii-ful, and designing Persons, taking Advantage ol such Defect of Jurisdiction, have, for many Years past, presumed to exercise the Business of an Apotheca y, within the Limitsaforesaid; and, under Colour therccf.^o make and compound sundry deceitful, adulterated, unmedicinable, and pernicious Medicines, which have been publickly fold and transmitted into all Parts of his Majesty's Dominions, in Defiance of the said Letters Patent; and that the said Empiricks, by making use of damaged, improper, or luppofititious Ingredients, are enabled not only to undersell the regular Apothecary (who faithfully pursues the Directions of the College, and the P.cscriptiui'is of Physicians) but to fell their Preparations for life than the prime Cost of the genuine Materials, of which the feme are pretended to be compounded, whereby many Persons are induced to purchase great Quantities of adulterated Medicines, not only to the Discredit of regular Pharmacy, and the Prejudice of the fair Trader, but to the manifest Hazard and Disadvantage of the Publick; and that, for preventing the like Mischiefs in the Practice both of Physick and Surgery, the Legislature have thought proper to reilrain all Persons whatsoever from the Exercise of either of those Professions, within the Limits above-mentioned, unless first examined and approved by the respective Governors of the College of Physicians, or Company of Surgeons: And therefore, as the Petitioners humbly conceive it to be of equal {if not of greater) C011-sequence to the Publick, that all ignorant and unskilful Persons should be restrained from preparing or vending Medicines, and that the Imposition of all damaged, adulterated, and pernicious Drugs and Medicines should be prevented, praying the House to rake the Premises into Consideration; and to grant such Remedy therein, as to the House shall appear necessary and expedient.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred 10 the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the feme, with their Opinion thereupon, to the House:

Tint the Town of Buckingham, from whence the County of that Name is denominated, was, in ancient Times, the Place where all the County Business was transaded, and where the Judges held the Assizes; but that for many Years patt it hath been usual, for the more convenient Administration of Justice to his Majesty's Subjects residing at the different Ends of the County, which is of a great Length, to appoint the Summer Assizes only, to be holden for the said County, at Buckingham, and the Winter Assizes at Aylesbury, and that the Petitioners, to their great Concern and Surprize, have seen this Regulation, which has been invariably pursued for many Years, lately brol en in upon, by an Appointment for holding the last Summer Assizes at Aylesbury, which was accordingly done:. And therefore praying the House to take the Premises into their Consideration; and give Leave that a Bill may be brought in for restoring to them the Summer Assizes, and fixing them there for the future.

That, by an Act of Parliament, made in the 9th and 10th Years of the Reign oftlie late King W the Third, intituled, An Act for erecting Hospitals and Workhouses within the City and County of the City of Exon, and for the better employing and maintaining the Poor there, the Mayor and Aldermen of the said City,

for the Time being, and Forty other Persons to be chosen, for the Time being, as in the Act is mentioned, were incorporated into One Body Politick and Corporate, by the Name of the Governor, Deputy Governor, Assistants, and Guardians of the Poor, of the City and County of Exon, with Power to purchase or erect any I Iospitals, Workhouscs, or Houses of Correction, and to let to work the Poor of the said City, and to compel ail idle or poor People, begging, or seeking Relief, to work, and to provide for all such other Poor, as, by any Laws then in Force, ought to be maintained or provided for, by any Parish or Place within the said City and County; and to raise, for the building and erecting such Hospital-, Work-houses, or 1 loutls of Correction, what Sum or Sums of Money should be needful, lb that the same shouldnot exceed the.Sum of Three thousand Pounds; and also, to raise what weekly, monthly, or other Sums should be needful for the Maintenance of the Poor in the said Hof* pitah, Workhouscs, or Houfis of Correction, or within the Care of the said Corp nation, foas the same did not exceed what had been paid in the salt! City and County towards the Maintenance of the Poor thereof, in any One of the Three then bit p:accding Years; and also, from time to time, under their common Seal, to certify unto the Mayor and justices for the said City and County, for the Time being, what Sum or Sums of Money should be requisite for the Maintenance of the Poor of the said City, the same to be levied in such manner, as by tire said Act is directe 1: And representing to the House, That in pursuance of the said Act, One Hospita) or Workhouse was toon after crcfted within the County of the said City, and the said Sum of Three thousand Pounds raised within the Space of Three Years so; and towards the erecting the rein; but that the Charges of the lard Building greatly exceeding the said Three thousand Pounds over and beyond several Benefactions of charitable disposed Persons, the said Corporation contracted a large Debt, l'ome Part of which hath been since dd'Cunsd, but that there dill re-mains due from the said Corporation, on Bonds, under their common Seal, the Sum of One thousand Three hundred l'uty-two Pounds Six Shillings, with Intcrelf for the same for upwards of Seven Years lad pad, amounting to uj wards of Five hundred Pounds: And further setting forth. That, ever since the obtaining the said Act unto this d ime, the said Corporation have certified yearly to the Mayor and Judiees of the said City and County, for thcTime being. That the Sum ot Two thousand Nine hundred Pounds was requisite and necessary for the Maintenance of the Poor of the said Hospital or Workhousc, or within the Care of the said Corporation; which laid Sum of Two thousand Nine hundred Pounds was the.utmod which the said Corporation were enabled, by the said Act, to levy or raise within the Space of any One Year; and which said Sum, or so much thereof as could be levied and raised, hath been expended, from time to time, for the Purposes in the said Act mentioned; but that, abouc Eight Years since, by rc ilon of several extreme hard Winters and dry Summers luccecding, and a general Slackness of Trade, for Five Years fucceliively, and the Dear-ness and Scarcity of Provisions, the Charge of maintaining the said Poor was greatly increased beyond the said Sum of Two thousand Nine hundred Pounds; so that the said Corporati m were obliged to contract a large Debt, as well for Money advanced by several of the Guardians, for the Use of the Poor of the said City, as also to Tradesmen, for Provisions and other NeccH'aries lor supporting the Poor in the said Hospital or Workhouse, to the Amount of the Sum of Three thousand One hundred Sixty-one Pounds and upwards; and that the Petitioners were in hopes to lnve lessened the said Debt in the succeeding Years, the Price ol Provisions havingcor.fulerably decreased, but that t he Petitioners find, by the experience of the Three hit Years, that though the said Sum, directed by the said A cl to be laved, has proved lb trident for the Maintenance of the Poor within the said l'hree Years, yet, by reason of the growing Interest on the said Bonds, as also of the Monies advanced by wdl-disposed Persons, VoL. 25.

for the Use of the Grid Corporation, in the Times aforesaid, as also that Actions have been commenced, and prosecuted to Judgment, against the said Corporation, by several Tradesmen, for divers Sums, really and bond side due to them from the said Corporation, for Provisions by them delivered, for the Use of the Poor in the said Hospital or Workhouse, the Debt of the said Corporation hath been gradually increased, even within the said last Three Years; and that the Petitioners have no Hope of discharging the fame, but by the Assistance of this House: and further representingto the House, That although, in con-fcquenceof the Certificates made by the said Corporation, under their common Seal, to the Mayor and J^uflices of the said City, Rates were made, from time to time, for the Levying of the said Sum of Two thousand Nine hundred Pounds yearly, yet as, by the said Act, an Appeal to the Justices of the Peace of the said City and County, at their next general Quarter-Seliions of the Peace after such. Assessment made and demanded, is given to any Person or Persons who should find him or themfehves unequally taxed or assessed, and the said Justices of the Peace had full Power and Authority to grant them Relief therein, many Appeals, from time to time, have been made, and Relief granted; and as neither the said Justices in the said Quarter-Sessions, nor the said Corporation) had any Power, by the said Act, to make a Re-act'eflrnent of such Sums as were so abated, or were otherwise deficient in the Sum certified as aforesaid, the said Corporation have never been able to levy and raise the Sum so by them yearly certified to the Mayor and Justices aforesaid; and there is now an Arrear to the said Corporation, by means of the said Deficiencies, which have gradually accrued, during the Existence of the said Corporation, the Sum of Three thousand Six hundred and Nine Pounds and upwards: And further representing to the House, That the Realons which appear to the Petitioners to have been the Cause of the said Deficiencies, and also of the Incurring of the great Debt as aforesaid, have been as follows; to wit, That, by the said Act, the Church-wardens and Overseers of the Poor, who have been directed to make the Assessments for levying the Sum certified as necessary to be raised, have rated as well all vacant Houses as those which were inhabited, by which means the Rates so charged on the said vacant Houses have proved to be deficient, no Distress having been pof-lible to be levied, whereby the same might be recovered; and for that several Persons, who have been rated, have removed from their Houses within the Year, and gone into other Parishes or Places in the County of , or elsewhere, so that such Rates could not be collected from such Persons, for the Residue of such Years: and also. That, by the said Act, the Powers for levying Distress have not been found sufficient to recover the Sums rated, even in Cafes where, by the Powers in the Act, commonly called the Land Tax Act, the Sums rated might have been recovered; and also, for that the Forty Persons chosen into the said Corporation as aforesaid, and on whom the Burthen of the Execution of the said Act chiefly lieth, are elected for Life; which hath deterred many Persons, who might otherwise have done great Service in the said Corporation, from engaging the rein; and for that no adequate Penalty is established by the said Act, against any Person chosen as a Member of the said Corporation, who shall neglect or refule toast; and for that, although the said Sum to be raised is, by the said Act, required to be raised and levied by Taxation of ever}' Inhabitant, and of all Lands, Houses, Tythes impropriate, Appropriation of Tythes, and all Stocks and Estates, in the said City and County, in equal Proportion, according to their respective Worths and Values, yet hitherto no Proportion between the landed and personal Estates hath been possible to be settled, nor is likely so to be, without the Interpolation of the Legislature: And therefore praying the Assistance of the House, and that Leave may be given to bring in a Bill to enable the Petitioners to levy the said Sum of Three thousand Six hundred and Nine Pounds, now in Arrear, by reason of such Deficiencies as aforesaid, within the Space of Three "Years, to be applied towards the

Wdtminster A Petition of the Commissioners for building a Bridge tiridge. at Westminster, being offered to be presented to the House i

Mr. Chancellor of the Exchequer, by his Majesty's Command, acquainted the House, That his Majesty,

having been informed of the Contents of the said Petition, recommends it to the Consideration of the House: Then the said Petition was brought up, and read; letting forth, That the Petitioners are, by several Acts of Parliament passed in his present Majesty's Reign, appointed Commissioners for building a J Bridge cross the River Thames, from the City of Westminster, to the opposite Shore; in the County of Suand are by Two Acts, passed im the 12th and 13th Years of his present Majesty's Reign, impowered to make, design, and lay out, such Ways, Streets, and Passages, as they shall find proper to make, open, and lay out, on each Side the River Thames, to and from the intended Bridge, the Courts of Justice, both Houses of Parliament, and the Parts adjacent; and to agree for and purchase such Houses and Ground, within certain Limits by the said Acts prescribed, as they shall find necessary for them to be possessed of; and that the Petitioners have madea considerableProgress in building the said Bridge, and have pu'rchafed several Houses and Parcels of Ground for opening, widening, and rendering convenient, the said Ways, Streets, and Passages; in doing which, they have expended almost: all the Monies hitherto granted them for the said Purposes (notwithstanding the y have proceeded with the utmost Care and Frugality), and are still under Contracts for several Parts of the Works which are now carrying on, and for purchasing several Estates necessary for the said Purposes, and which will amount to a greater Sum than is now in the Hands of the Petitioners; and that the Petitioners find themselves under a Necessity of applying to this House for such farther Sums of Money as the House shall judge proper, that a Work so useful and advantageous to the Publick may not be Hopped for want thereof: And therefore praying, That the House will take the Premises into Consideration; and grant the Petitioners such further Sums of Money as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered, That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of the Committee of the whole House, to whom it is referred to consider further of the Supply granted to his Majesty.

A PETITION of the Trustees, whose Names are thereunto subscribed, appointed to put in Execution an Act of Parliament, paired in the Tenth Year of the Reign of his present Majesty King the Second, for repairing the Road from Hntford Bridge Hi// to the Town of Baftngstoke, and also the Road from Hertford Bridge Hill aforesaid to the Town of Odikam, in the County of Southampton, was presented to the House, and read; letting forth. That, by the said Act, several Toils and Duties were granted and made payable, for repairing the said Road; which said Act was to take place, and have Continuance only, from and after the First Day of June 1737, for and during the Term of Twenty-one Tears; and that the Petitioners, finding the said Roads in a very ruinous Condition, and the annual Income not being sufficient, have been obliged to borrow a considerable Sum of Money for putting the same into, and keeping the same in Repair; and that the Sum of Twelve hundred Pounds Principal Money is now due on the Credit of the said Act; which, with the Income of the said Toll collected, hath been duly paid and applied for the Interest of the Money borrowed, and in repairing the said Road; and that by means of the great Length of the Roads directed by the said Act to be repaired, and the many heavy Carriages passing through the fame, the said Roads are now in a very ruinous Condiiion, and cannot be effectually amended and kept in good Repair for the foture; and that the Money due on the Credit of the subsisting Term cannot be repaid without the Aid of a farther Act of Parliament: And praying, That Leave may be given to bring in a Bill for enlarging the Term and Powers granted by the said Act, for so long Time, and in such Manner, as to the House shall seem meet.

Ordered That the said Petition be referred to the Consideration of a Committee: And that they do examine the Matter thereof; and report the fame, as it shall appear to them, to the House:

Mr. Secretary at War, by his Majesty's Command, Convention presented to the House, with Duke of

Copy of the Subsidiary Convention between his Majesty Brunswick. and the States General, on the one Part; and the Duke of Brunswick IVolfenbuttle, on the other; signed at the Hague, the First of February 1748, N. S.; and,

Translation: And also,

Estimate of the Charge of Four thousand Eight hundred Foot, the Troops of his most Serene Highness the Duke of Brunswick Wolfenbuttle, taken into the Pay of Great Britain and the States General, fro;p the 25th of

March 1748, to the 24th December following, both inclusive.

And the Titles of the said Papers were read.

The said Copy is bound up with the other Papers of this Sefixon.

And the said Translation and Estimate are as followeth; viz.

Treaty, by virtue of which his most Serene Highness the Duke of Brunswick Wolfenbuttle yields to the Pay of his Majesty the King of Great Britairt, and to their High Mightinesse the Lords the States General of the United Provinces of the Low,

a Body of 4,800 Men, Infantry.

Art. Ift.

His most Serene Highness the Duke of Brunswick Wolfenbuttle engages to furnish to his Majesty,

and to their High Mightinelfes, a Body of 4,800 Men, which consist in Six Regiments of Foot, each Regiment of Eight Companies, and each Company of an Hundred Men, with a Great Staff for each Regiment: His most Serene Highness shall furnidi, over and above that, an Artillery Company, and Eight Field Pieces, attended with their Train Horses, and proper necessary Requisites; the Whole provided with a General Staff', proportionable to what is more fully specified in the Lift hereto annexed.

' Art. m

As the said Troops shall be, at their Arrival, duly clothed, armed, exercised, and furnished in general with every thing necessary to be employed in the Field, his most Serene Highness (Hall continue to supply, for this Purpose, every thing at his Cost, by virtue of this Treaty.

Art. III".

The said Body of Troops shall be regularly and readily paid upon the Foot, and according to what is marked in the Lift mentioned in the ift Article, and inserted at the End of this Treaty; for One Half, by his Britannick Majesty*

t

16° Februarii. ^.1747.

Contention Majesty; and, for the other Half, by their High Mighti-Bruni^'ick nc^es» ^'s Majesty and their High Mightinesse reciprocally guarantying to his moil Serene Highness the Quote Parts which each of the Confederates shall have to pay to his most Serene Highness, as well by virtue of this Article, as of all those which follow

The Forage shall be delivered , from the Magazines of his Britannick Majesty and their High Mightiness, to those Troops, according to the Lift inserted at the End of this Treaty, from the time that the said Troops shall take the Field, till they shall return into Garrison, or into Winter Quarters, excepting the Time that the allied Army shall forage; at which time Care shall be had to procure to thelc Troops the same Conveniences, and the same Advantages, as to the Republick's own Troops.

The Bread mail be furnished, during the Campaign, to these Troops, in paying for it at the Prices of the Contraft; but in case that the Portion of Bread, at the Rate of Two Pounds, should cost theft Troops above One and One-third of a Stiver, or Four Stivers, Dutch Money, the Three Portions, or Six Pounds of Bread, his Britannick Majesty and their High Mightinesse shall make good this Overplus to the Contractors, and reimburse also the Expences to be incurred for the Waggons serving to transport the Sick, the Passages by Rivers, the Wood, and the Straw, and other Dependencies of this Nature: The said necessary Wood and Straw shall likewise be delivered gratis during the Campaign, as well as all the necessary Ammunitions for this Body; the Whole, according to the Proportion established between his Britannick Majesty and their High Mightinesse for the casual Expences of the War; guarantying mutually, that each of them shall cause Provision to be made in every thing as above.

The Payment of the Quote Part of their High Mighti-nesses shall be made at the Counting-houses, without the least Deduction; and the Generals, Officers of the Great Staff, and the Captains, shall be dispensed from paying the Leges or AElen-Gelder.

Art. IVA.

The laid TTbops, as well as their Generals, shall take the Oath of Fidelity to his Britannick Majesty and their High Mightinesse, according to the Formulary used with the Hessian Troops, without prejudicing that which

they have taken to his most Serene Highness the Duke of Brunswick Wolfcnbuttlt\ and shall follow the Orders of his Britannick Majesty and of their High Mightinesse, to be employed as the Service of the common Cause shall require.

Art. V,h.

The said Body of Six Battalions shall put themselves in Motion in Eight Weeks, or sooner, if it is possible, after the Signature of this Treaty; and shall use the greatest Diligence to arrive as soon as possible upon the Frontiers of the Republick, or at the allied Army, according as the Circumstances of the Times ft)all require.

Art. VP\

For this Purpose, his Britannick Majesty and their High

Mightinesse shall immediately fend One or Two Com-tniffaries to receive the said Body, muster it, administer to it the Oath of Fidelity, and conduct it into the States of the United Provinces, or to the allied Army, according as the Circumstances of the Times shall require.

Art. VIP.

His most Serene Highness the Duke of Brunswick IVol-fenbuttle reserves to himself the Disposal of all the Polls, without Exception, which may become vacant in this Body; the Administration of Justice remaining also reserved to him.

Art. VIIIth.

His Britannick Majesty and their High Mightinesse shall cause the necessary requisitorial Letters to be dispatch for all the Marches of the said Troops; and shall always assign them, as much as can be, the most convenient and least difficult Routs.

Art. IXth.

His Britannick Majesty and their High Mightinesse shall be at Liberty to have the said Body of Troops muf-7

teredeverv Yew, on the iftof the Month of April\ and his Majesty and their High Mightinesse shall not be obliged to pay for what shall be then wanting of the said Body; with a Reservation of the Absent on account of Iliness certified, or for other good Reasons, of which his Britannick Majesty and their High Mightinesse shall be the Judges.

Art. Xth.

If, after the Campaign is ended, his Britannick Majesty and their High Mightinesse find, that the Reason of War permits that these Troops, or a Part of them, return home in order to recruit those Troops, which shall pal's the Winter in the Country of his most Serene Highness shall not the less enjoy their Pay, and the Advantages which the National Troops of the States General of the United Provinces enjoy, in order to enable them to recruit at the End of each Campaign.

The Troops which shall remain during the Winter in Garrison in the Republick, or in the Countries subject to the Dominion of the Republick, or in the Law,

shall be treated in every thing, without Exception, as well Officers as Soldiers, as the National Troops of their High Mightinesse; the Whole at the Cods of his Majesty and of their High Mightinesse, according to the Proportion here above established.

Art. XP\

All the Recruits necessary for this Body being to be made in the hereditary Countries of his most Serene Highness the Duke of Brunswick IV, it is agreed on both Sides, that, from the Signature of this Treaty, and henceforward, until its Expiration, any Deserter from the Troops of his Britannick Majesty, or of the Republick, or who are in the Pay ®f the one or the other of the Two aforesaid Powers, shall not be received into this Body; and likewise that any Deserter of the said Body shall not be received amongst; the Troops of his Britannick Majesty, nor of their High Mightinesse, or who are in the Pay of the one or of the other of the aforesaid Two Powers; but that they shall be faithfully restored on both Sides, excepting however all the Deserters who shall be found engaged, before the Date of this Treaty, in the Troops of the one or the other of the contracting Powers, which shall not be reclaimed on any account.

And, to the end that his most Serene Highness may keep this Body of Troops always in a complete State, his Britannick Majesty and their High Mightinesse engage to pay for each Company, as well of Artillery as Infantry, 1,000 Florins Dutch Money.

Art. XIP\

The Losses sustained in the Field in Men and Horses belonging to the Field Artillery, in an Action with the Enemy, shall be made good at the Expence of his Britannick Majesty and of their High Mightinesse, each for the Troops which it pays, upon the most favourable Foot, whether of national or foreign Troops in the Service of his Britannick Majesty and of their High M ightinesses; with this Distinction, nevertheless, that if One of the said Regiments sustainsa Loss altogether extraordinary, either in a Battle, Attack, or Siege, or by an uncommon contagious Sickness, his Britannick Majesty and their High Mightinesse shall have all possible Regard thereto, and shall make good, in the most equitable manner, the Lois either of the Officer or of* the Soldier,

Art. XIII,fc.

His Britannick Majesty and their High Mightinesse shall cause to be paid to his most Serene Highness Thirty Crowns current Money of H,under the Denomination of Inlisting-money for each Soldier clot lied and duly armed, comprehending therein the Drums and Bas Officers; which Payment shall be made at the Hague, in ready Money, by his Britannick Majesty, for one Half, and their High Mightinesse for the other Half; to wit. One Half of the Sum total, immediately after the Signa- . ture of the present Treaty, to the Person authorized lor that Purpose by his most Serene Highness; and the ether Half when the said Body of Troops shall be delivered to the Commissaries of his Britannick Majesty and of their High Mightinesse; on Condition, however, that Thirty Crowns shall be retained for each Soldier, who, without

consumed by the great Fire in 1666; and King Charles the Second being desirous the same might be rebuilt in a more magnificent Manner, the Petitioners contributed equally with the City of London, in the purchasing of Ground for making the Exchange more commodious, and in rebuilding the fame; whereby, and by the Money advanced to the King and Parliament, the Petitioners not only expended several large Sums, which had been given them for charitable Purposes, but also contracted a considerable Debt: That, in 1698, Doctor Asheton made a Proposal to the Petitioners, to take in Subscriptions for the Granting of Annuities, at the Rate of Thirty Pounds per Centum, to the Widows of Clergymen and others, commencing from the Death of the Subscribers; which he then vesselented would be of publick Utility, and of great Advantage to the Petitioners; and which they accepted, in hopes they should thereby discharge their Debts, and replace the charitable Donations which they
